payload.title: body_server: read-only `objects` op for viewers that mirror the world
payload.body:
A viewer that draws the duck's world — a browser mirroring the simulation, say — can rebuild the duck from `read`, but has no way to see the loose things in a scene: the balls and boxes in `scene_apartment.xml`. `read` deliberately carries only what a robot could sense, so this adds a separate op rather than widening it.

**Change** (`src/mjlab_microduck/sim/body_server.py`, +17 lines)

- `World` collects the loose bodies once at startup: every free joint whose name is not a duck's `trunk_base_freejoint` (so it holds for any number of ducks and any prefix).
- `World.objects()` answers `name -> [x, y, z, qw, qx, qy, qz]`, copied under the world lock exactly like `read`.
- `dispatch` serves it as `{"op": "objects"}` → `{"objects": {...}}`.

It writes nothing. A scene without loose things answers `{}`. Existing ops and their answers are unchanged, so `robotd --sim`, `tofd --sim` and the camera path are unaffected.

**Verification**

- `tests/test_body_server_objects.py` (new): lists the apartment's 7 loose bodies and not the duck; follows the live `qpos`; the op is served and leaves the state untouched; the default `scene.xml` answers empty.
- `uv run --with pytest pytest tests/`: 267 passed, 1 skipped (macOS, Apple silicon).
- Exercised for several days against `scripts/duck-sim` with `DUCK_SIM_SCENE=apartment`, polled at ~45 Hz alongside `robotd`'s 50 Hz `read` with no change to the loop rate.

**Context**: I use it in [microduck-companion](https://github.com/GC-RENCAO/microduck-companion), an unofficial LLM + webcam companion that mirrors the simulated duck and its apartment in a browser; when the duck kicks a ball, the ball now moves on screen too. Happy to rename the op or move it if you would rather keep viewer-facing calls elsewhere.

**Rollback**: revert the commit; nothing else depends on the op.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

payload.title: Fix shared rough-terrain configs and walking curriculum
payload.body:
Importing mjlab_microduck.tasks constructs both training and play configs.
The rough factories currently share MICRODUCK_ROUGH_TERRAINS_CFG, so creating
play configs changes the template and training configs to a 5 x 5 random grid.

Deep-copy the template in all four affected factories (Velocity, SitStand,
StandUp and GroundPick; VelStand inherits Velocity). Enable curriculum mode
for rough Velocity/VelStand training, while play keeps its 5 x 5 random grid.
This also covers their registered Backlash variants.

The shared template retains its declared 10 x 20 settings. mjlab 1.3.0 uses
one column per terrain type in curriculum mode, so the walking training
terrain actually generates 10 rows x 4 columns. SitStand, StandUp and
GroundPick retain random generation and regain their declared 10 x 20 grid.

Related to https://github.com/pollen-robotics/microduck_rl/issues/65.
Credit to @notwitcheer for the diagnosis and published walking-family fix:
https://github.com/notwitcheer/microduck-lab/blob/main/patches/terrain_curriculum_mode_patch.py
This extends isolation to the other affected factories and adds regression
tests for the reported bug.

Validation at develop b02fdea4902c2b93b7d34a83a6f05da4ececb7d3:

- The same 26 new regression cases fail against the original source and
  pass against the fixed source. Coverage includes task registration,
  train/play creation order, nested terrain settings and Backlash variants.
- Full CPU test suite: 289 passed, 1 skipped (linux-aarch64 GPU check).
- Seed-65 walking terrain: generated 10 x 4 patches, applied the existing
  contact-softening callback and compiled in CPU MuJoCo; 3,204 geoms and
  10 heightfields.
- Ruff checks pass for the new test, and git diff --check passes.

CUDA validation on Google Colab (Tesla T4, PyTorch CUDA 12.8), using a clean
checkout of PR commit 930dc02c5154f5e0c6a819f99ab6630ea45ac18b:

- `Mjlab-Velocity-Rough-MicroDuck`: 64 environments, 5 PPO iterations,
  seed 65, NaN guard enabled; all five iterations completed (7,680 environment steps).
- Saved configuration confirms `curriculum: true`, `num_rows: 10`,
  `num_cols: 20` and 64 environments. In curriculum mode this generates
  10 rows x 4 terrain-type columns, as described above.
- All 260 recorded TensorBoard scalar samples (52 tags across 5 iterations)
  were finite. The `nan_state` termination metric was zero at every iteration.
- Checkpoint `model_4.pt` exported through `scripts/export.py`; the Colab runner
  confirmed `[1,61] -> [1,14]` ONNX inference with finite output for a zero input.

Training behaviour changes: restoring the larger non-walking training grids
increases generated terrain geometry, and enabling the walking curriculum
changes its terrain distribution. GPU smoke coverage is limited to the rough
Velocity task. There is no comparative learning-quality evaluation or physical
robot test; this short run does not establish better policy performance. The
non-walking tasks' curriculum-mode decision is outside this candidate's scope.

payload.title: Add optional read-only MuJoCo visualization stream
payload.body:
## Motivation

`duck-body` owns the authoritative MuJoCo world, but developer tools currently have no supported way to observe that exact state without opening the desktop viewer or duplicating simulation logic. This adds an optional read-only image stream so dashboards and debugging tools can inspect the same world that drives `robotd`.

## What changed

- Add an optional visualization service behind `duck-body --render`.
- Serve cached JPEG or PNG frames through the existing TCP/NDJSON server.
- Add `render`, `camera`, and `render_config` operations for frame polling, orbit/zoom/reset controls, and runtime resolution, FPS, quality, and format changes.
- Copy `MjData` while holding the world lock, then render and encode outside the lock so slow software rendering does not block the 50 Hz physics/control loop.
- Support optional shutdown after the last render client remains disconnected.
- Keep Pillow in a dedicated `visualization` extra.
- Document the feature and add focused lifecycle, locking, validation, camera, configuration, and wire-adapter tests.

## Compatibility and scope

The feature is disabled by default. Existing `duck-body` operations and startup behavior remain unchanged. It does not modify robot models, physics, training, reward design, policy inference, observation/action layouts, or authoritative simulator state. Camera and render configuration affect only the read-only visualization stream.

## What this enables

- Browser-based simulation dashboards and live robot monitoring.
- Headless or remote inspection of the authoritative MuJoCo scene.
- Recording, debugging, and automated visual regression tooling.
- Additional read-only developer clients without embedding or duplicating simulator logic.

## Validation

- `uv lock --check`
- `uv run --locked --extra visualization --with pytest pytest tests/` — 211 passed, 1 skipped
- `uv run --with ruff ruff check src/mjlab_microduck/sim/body_server.py src/mjlab_microduck/sim/visualization tests/test_visualization.py`
- End-to-end Studio → robotd → policy → MuJoCo contract probe

payload.title: v8 velstand: inconsistent pure lateral starts and yaw drift in MuJoCo/Warp CPU
payload.body:
# v8 velstand: inconsistent pure lateral starts and yaw drift in MuJoCo/Warp CPU

Hi, I am investigating inconsistent pure lateral motion with the released v8 `velstand.onnx` policy. This may be related to #59, although that report and its simulator results mainly concern v5.

I am reporting observations and asking for configuration guidance. I have not established a source-code defect or tested this on a physical robot.

## Environment

- Policy: `pollen-robotics/microduck-policies`, revision `v8`, `velstand.onnx`.
- Policy SHA256: `2fc7f8ee6acd7d0d3f66a99927b5d5a56589aeed02ec714de329b252d5ccf492`.
- Local base checkout: `b26950afb74432b53fe81c4d322988a3785ea0a6`, with local diagnostic changes.
- macOS / arm64; Warp CPU, no CUDA GPU.
- MuJoCo 3.10.0, mjlab 1.3.0, warp-lang 1.12.0, Torch 2.9.1, NumPy 2.4.1, ONNX Runtime 1.24.4.
- BAM pinned to `62bd8ce12154340be97e06f7f41a0ca8f116d967`.
- Physics 200 Hz; deterministic ONNX inference 50 Hz; 61 actor observations and 14 actions. The published policy weights were unchanged.

## Diagnostic setup and limitations

**This is a locally modified diagnostic configuration derived from VelStand, not an untouched upstream task.**

It uses flat terrain and the all-collisions/backlash robot with BAM. It starts upright at root z=0.125m / yaw=0, disables prone initialization and injected pushes, and fixes head/body commands to zero. Domain randomization, actor observation corruption and IMU mounting error are disabled; BAM voltage is 7.4V with drop gain 0.1. Physics uses 5ms implicitfast, 30 solver iterations and 50 line-search iterations. Physical command/sensor delays remain enabled.

The local wrapper also changes rewards, termination settings and critic observations; no training or critic inference was performed, and no falls or environment resets occurred during this probe.

The policy was evaluated directly in the mjlab/MuJoCo Warp environment, bypassing Studio, HTTP controls and robotd. No external heading controller or added yaw command was used. These results come from **three parallel environments with one seed (0)**, not three independent seeds.

## Command sequence

Command axes are `[vx, vy, vyaw]`; head/body commands remain zero:

1. Stand: `[0, 0, 0]` for 2s.
2. Left: `[0, +0.3, 0]` for 10s.
3. Stop for 3s.
4. Right: `[0, -0.3, 0]` for 10s.
5. Stop for 3s.
6. Left again: `[0, +0.3, 0]` for 10s.

## Observed results

Displacements and yaw excursions are measured relative to the trunk heading at the beginning of each segment. Maximum yaw is the largest absolute yaw departure during the entire 10s segment.

| Environment | Initial left displacement | Right displacement | Right maximum yaw excursion | Left after right displacement |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | +0.0063m | -0.5302m | 13.40° | +0.4706m |
| 1 | +0.0062m | -0.5450m | 10.26° | +0.4435m |
| 2 | +0.4657m | -0.5375m | 16.54° | +0.0066m |

Three of the nine lateral segments barely moved; the other six did move. The main observations are inconsistent initiation and yaw drift under zero commanded yaw. I am not claiming that every segment is immobile or that a local acceptance threshold is an official requirement.

## Questions

1. Is reliable pure lateral motion from rest (`vx=0, vy=±0.3, vyaw=0`) expected with the released v8 VelStand policy?
2. Are there recommended scene, BAM, voltage, action-filtering or command settings for reproducing this checkpoint's lateral behavior?
3. Could the nominal evaluation changes or Warp CPU backend explain these observations? Is there a known-good upstream reproduction command/configuration to compare against?

I would like to verify configuration compatibility before attributing this to the policy or training recipe. The numerical report can be attached as `v8-lateral-observations.json`; its pass/fail fields use local diagnostic limits, not official criteria. The existing local probe depends on local configuration modules, so it is not yet a standalone upstream reproduction script.

[v8-lateral-observations.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33923720/v8-lateral-observations.json)

payload.title: apartment scene: ToF beams into the stairwell pass under the floor slab and read "no target"
payload.body:
In `scene_apartment.xml` the stairwell (x ∈ [-0.40, 0.00], y ∈ [-1.40, -0.70]) has steps but no walls or bottom, and the floors around it are 1 cm slabs over empty space. A downward ToF beam that enters the hole at a shallow angle misses the steps, passes under the slab beyond, and hits nothing — so `sim/tof.py` reports status 255 ("nothing in range") where a real VL53L8CX would measure the stairwell's wall or bottom.

Repro, sensor at standing height over the north corridor, looking south:

```python
import numpy as np, mujoco
m = mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_path("src/mjlab_microduck/robot/microduck/scene_apartment.xml")
d = mujoco.MjData(m); mujoco.mj_forward(m, d)
g = np.zeros(1, dtype=np.int32)
for el in (8.4, 14.1, 19.7):                      # rows 5-7 of the 8x8 grid, head level
    e = np.radians(el); v = np.array([0, -np.cos(e), -np.sin(e)])
    print(el, mujoco.mj_ray(m, d, np.array([-0.2, -0.25, 0.246]), v, None, 1, -1, g))
# 8.4 -> 1.657 (floor beyond the hole)   14.1 -> -1.0   19.7 -> -1.0
```

Why it matters: a cliff guard developed in the simulator only ever sees the "nothing in range" signature of a drop; on the robot it would see a longer range instead. Both should be handled, but only one can be tested here.

A possible fix, five boxes lining the hole 0.6 m deep:

```xml
<geom name="well_bottom" type="box" size="0.20 0.35 0.005" pos="-0.20 -1.05 -0.605"/>
<geom name="well_n" type="box" size="0.20 0.005 0.30" pos="-0.20 -0.695 -0.30"/>
<geom name="well_s" type="box" size="0.20 0.005 0.30" pos="-0.20 -1.405 -0.30"/>
<geom name="well_w" type="box" size="0.005 0.35 0.30" pos="-0.405 -1.05 -0.30"/>
<geom name="well_e" type="box" size="0.005 0.35 0.30" pos="0.005 -1.05 -0.30"/>
```

With them the same beams read 1.186 m and 1.221 m (the south wall). Checked against `develop` @ 8d0db74 with MuJoCo directly; I haven't run the full training or the policies with the change.

Found while building a drop detector for an autonomy client: https://github.com/samoxis/microduck-brain (fixtures with these frames in `tests/fixtures/mujoco_drop.json`).

payload.title: [Bug] Viser viewer crashes for Roulade task due to invalid slider range
payload.body:
### Description

Hi! I trained the Velocity and Roulade policies locally and ran into an issue when trying to visualize Roulade using the Viser browser viewer.

The native MuJoCo viewer works, but Viser crashes during initialization.

### Steps to reproduce

Run with a trained Roulade checkpoint:

```bash
uv run play Mjlab-Roulade-Flat-MicroDuck \
    --wandb-run-path ENTITY/PROJECT/RUN_ID \
    --viewer viser
```

### Error

```text
File "mjlab/tasks/velocity/mdp/velocity_command.py", line 166, in create_gui
    max_input = server.gui.add_slider(...)

File "viser/_gui_api.py", line 1900, in add_slider
    assert max >= value >= min

AssertionError
```

### Root cause

The Roulade environment uses very small velocity command ranges:

```python
command.ranges.lin_vel_x = (-0.01, 0.01)
command.ranges.lin_vel_y = (-0.01, 0.01)
command.ranges.ang_vel_z = (-0.05, 0.05)
```

However, `mjlab` creates joystick sliders with `min=0.1` and `initial_value=max_val`, which fails when `max_val < 0.1`.

### Suggested fix

Since Roulade doesn't need interactive velocity commands, one option is to skip joystick GUI creation for tasks with near-zero command ranges.

Alternatively, the slider initialization could be fixed upstream in `mjlab` to support smaller ranges.

I tested a workaround by overriding `VelocityCommandCommandOnly.create_gui()` to skip the joystick sliders when any upper bound is below `0.1`. **Viser now works correctly.**

```python
def create_gui(self, *args, **kwargs) -> None:
    """Skip joystick GUI for tasks with near-zero commands."""
    upper_bounds = (
        self.cfg.ranges.lin_vel_x[1],
        self.cfg.ranges.lin_vel_y[1],
        self.cfg.ranges.ang_vel_z[1],
    )

    if any(bound < 0.1 for bound in upper_bounds):
        return

    super().create_gui(*args, **kwargs)
```

### Environment

- Windows 10 + WSL2 (Ubuntu)
- Python 3.12
- NVIDIA RTX 5050 Laptop GPU
- `mjlab==1.3.0`
- `warp-lang==1.12.0`

Thanks for the great project!

payload.title: feat: add MicroDuck 2.0 simulation and trainer
payload.body:
## Summary

- Add a selectable microduck2 MuJoCo body profile with a provisional 45 cm, 3.2 kg reference body and a low-obstacle scene.
- Keep the body-server protocol compatible while preventing accidental use of alpha policies with the new body.
- Add a small offline, reviewed-feedback trainer for the behavior-affect selector used by the companion runtime proposal.

## Scope and safety

This is a simulation/research proposal, not a deployable robot policy. The reference MJCF uses primitive geometry pending reviewed CAD exports and measured actuator data. The trainer produces affect-selection data only; it cannot command motors, enable skills, or update a physical robot.

## Validation

- python -m py_compile src/mjlab_microduck/sim/body_server.py
- XML structural parsing for the microduck2 robot and scene
- git diff --check

Full MuJoCo execution and policy training were not run here because the required GPU/runtime environment is not installed on this Windows host.

payload.title: feat: Windows 10 support
payload.body:
## Overview

### 1. Route torch to the CUDA 12.6 index on Windows

On Windows, PyPI's torch wheel is CPU-only (`torch.version.cuda is None`), so training finds no GPU. torch is now routed to the cu126 index on win32, matching the local NVIDIA driver (560.x / CUDA 12.6) and the Pascal sm_61 GPU. `uv.lock` has been re-resolved.

Related: MuJoCo Warp's dense/Newton path relies on MathDx `tile_cholesky`, which only supports sm_70+, and fails to compile on Pascal (sm_61). `tasks/__init__.py` now falls back to a sparse Jacobian + CG solver on pre-Volta GPUs.

### 2. Decode Windows arrow/function keys

On Windows, arrow/function keys don't arrive as ESC escape sequences but as a NUL or 0xE0 prefix byte followed by a scan code (up/down/right/left = H/P/M/K). `infer_policy.py` now reads keys via `msvcrt` when `termios`/`tty` are unavailable and decodes these scan codes.

### 3. Other Windows compatibility fixes

- Tests read `pyproject.toml` / `uv.lock` / sources with explicit UTF-8 (Windows defaults to the ANSI codepage)
- Skip the Unix console-script content check on win32 (compiled `.exe` launchers)
- Add `.idea` to `.gitignore`
- New `notebook.md`: local visualization quick-reference (PowerShell-friendly, covering viewer backend selection, backtick line continuation, and the mandatory `--new-cmd-obs` for the 61D policies)

payload.title: Walking policy won't start slow walk from stand still
payload.body:
Hi! I've been setting up `duck-sim` and noticed the duck wouldn't walk when I asked for a slow walk. It just stands there. I dug in a bit and I think it's the shipped v5 policies rather than anything in the runtime.

From a standstill, both `alpha_walking.onnx` and `velstand.onnx` refuse to take a step below about 0.22 m/s, even though training samples `lin_vel_x` from `(-0.4, 0.4)`. What surprised me is that it happens in the training env too. I ran the ONNX in `Mjlab-Velocity-Flat-MicroDuck` with a pinned twist command (32 envs, mean forward speed in m/s):

| cmd vx | play cfg as is | play cfg, pushes off | `velstand`, pushes off |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.15 | 0.078 | **0.007** (1/32 walking) | **0.002** (0/32) |
| 0.20 | – | 0.071 (10/32) | 0.021 (1/32) |
| 0.30 | 0.146 | 0.144 | 0.141 |

I think the reason nobody's caught it is that in-sim play pushes the robot every 0.5–1.0 s, and each push nudges it into stepping. So in play it looks fine. Once it's moving it'll happily keep going at 0.15. It just can't *start* slow. I see the same thing in `scripts/infer_policy.py` and through `robotd --sim`, so it doesn't look like a sim2sim gap.

It feels related to #46, but this one is about the policies people are running right now.

A few ideas, in case they're useful:

- **Evaluate with pushes off.** The export/publish check, or a quick play mode, could command a slow speed from rest with pushes disabled, so this shows up before a set ships.
- **Look at the forward-only share.** The base cfg has `rel_forward_envs=0.2` with forward-only commands clamped to `vx >= 0.3`, so a chunk of training never sees slow forward walking. I haven't verified this is the cause, though.
- **More episodes starting at rest.** Episodes that begin from a standstill with a small nonzero command would teach it to break into a walk at low speed.


Tested on `develop` @ `cb70b79`, `seed-v5`

payload.title: [Checkpoint request] Exact .pt behind alpha_walking (441tzs6d@3750) and current v8 VelStand
payload.body:
Hi Pollen Robotics RL Team,

We are running controlled continued-training experiments on Microduck, including left-right symmetry ablations, on a local workstation. To compare against an exact official baseline rather than a different training lineage, we are looking for the original PyTorch checkpoint used to export the official walking policy.

## Target policy and documented provenance

Our archived official Hub file is:

- Repository: `pollen-robotics/microduck-policies`
- Revision: `1b56c396825c052a4e26e95cf2b8d8298af9e9b4`
- File: `alpha_walking.onnx`
- Size: 793,705 bytes
- SHA-256: `e36332d383997d51401897734cd3e79cf5038406feddb18b4d57ecfb141daa6c`

The same bytes were archived as `BEST_alpha_walking.onnx` from the official Microduck simulator. The repository documentation identifies this policy's source as W&B run `pollen-robotics/mjlab_microduck/441tzs6d`, checkpoint `model_3750.pt`.

## Why the ONNX export cannot provide an exact PPO resume

We reproduced the deterministic actor from the ONNX export, including its MLP weights and baked observation normalization, with zero output difference on 13,056 recorded observations.

However, the ONNX export does not preserve several checkpoint states needed to reproduce the original PPO state exactly:

- critic weights;
- Adam optimizer state;
- stochastic policy `distribution.std_param`;
- observation-normalizer sample `count`;
- training iteration and `common_step_counter`.

These values can be reinitialized or assumed, but they cannot be recovered exactly from the ONNX file. We therefore classify such a reconstruction as a new actor warm-start lineage, not a continuation of the official run.

As a local feasibility check, we trained only a fresh critic while keeping the reconstructed actor frozen. Our preregistered local validation gate remained unmet after 120 iterations (reported EV approximately 0.398 and NRMSE approximately 0.776, against thresholds of 0.80 and 0.45). We did not start PPO. These figures explain why we did not treat the reconstruction as an exact baseline resume; they are not intended as a general claim that actor warm-starting cannot work.

## Request

Our primary request is the exact checkpoint behind the archived walking policy:

- W&B run: `pollen-robotics/mjlab_microduck/441tzs6d`
- Checkpoint: `model_3750.pt`
- Supporting material, if available: checkpoint SHA-256, exact source commit, and saved environment and runner parameter files.

Separately, if current production checkpoints can be shared, we would also appreciate:

- W&B run: `pollen-robotics/mjlab_microduck/0045i2si`
- Checkpoint: `model_2749.pt`
- Documented source commit: `3750776`
- Saved environment and runner parameter files.

We understand that the v8 VelStand checkpoint belongs to a different task and training lineage and is not a substitute for `441tzs6d@3750` in an alpha-walking symmetry comparison.

A direct download, a Hugging Face artifact, or read-only W&B access sufficient to download the checkpoint would all work.

Thank you for open-sourcing the Microduck RL stack and for any guidance you can provide.

payload.title: License: pin 3D model files to CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and scope it
payload.body:
## What

Pins the license of the 3D model files to **CC BY-NC-SA 4.0** and makes its scope explicit.

- **README**: the License section now names CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (canonical element order, with version), links it, and lists the covered paths.
- **LICENSE-MODELS.md** (new): scope, the Apache 2.0 status of everything else, and attribution requirements.
- **pyproject.toml**: `license = "Apache-2.0 AND CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0"` and `LICENSE-MODELS.md` added to `license-files`. The wheel ships 54 STL meshes, so its metadata should say so. Checked with `uv build --wheel`: both license files land in `dist-info/licenses/` and `License-Expression` reads `Apache-2.0 AND CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0`.
- **LICENSE** (Apache 2.0) is unchanged on purpose, so GitHub and PyPI keep detecting it.

## Why

The README said "Creative Commons BY-SA-NC" with no version and no file list. Creative Commons says a license reference must name both the license and the version, and recommends 4.0 over all earlier versions. A community member building a Microduck demo asked on Discord which version applies and whether the MJCF is covered; this PR answers both in the repo.

## Please check before merging

1. **MJCF scope.** This PR covers only the `.stl` meshes. The MJCF `.xml` files, `config_mjcf_*.json` and `.part` metadata stay under Apache 2.0. If the MJCF should be CC as well, add it to the list in `LICENSE-MODELS.md` and the README.
2. **Third-party geometry.** All `.part` files point to the same Onshape document and none are flagged as standard content, but some meshes look like vendor parts: `xl330` (ROBOTIS), `pcb__raspberry_pi_zero_2_w`, `seeed_bearing__*`, `np_f970`. If those were imported from vendor CAD, they may need to be excluded or credited separately.
3. **Same gap elsewhere.** `reachy_mini` uses the same unversioned "Creative Commons BY-SA-NC" line, so it likely needs the same fix.

payload.title: publish --timeline: upload a stage performance's timeline.json beside the policy
payload.body:
## What

`uv run publish --timeline FILE` stages the file as `timeline.json` next to `policy.onnx`, `manifest.json` and `README.md`. It is uploaded at the repo root in the same commit, or copied into `publish-<name>/` by `--dry-run`. `manifest.json` is unchanged, and without `--timeline` nothing changes.

## Why

On the Microduck Arena, MicroDuck Got a Talent (event id `swag-contest`) becomes a performance on a stage: the Arena plays the entry's `timeline.json` for up to 20 s. A timeline is a list of keyframes, each giving the 13 command numbers (twist, head, body) from its time on. The Arena validates the format. `publish` only refuses a file that is not UTF-8 JSON, read the way the Arena reads it, because microduck_rl does not depend on the Arena.

## Stacked on #57

The base is `challenge-recipe-publishing` (#57), the branch microduck-challenges locks, so this diff holds only the two `--timeline` commits.

## Tests

`tests/test_publish_manifest.py`: 56 passed. Three tests are new:
- a dry run stages `timeline.json` byte for byte and leaves the manifest alone;
- a file that is not JSON is refused before anything is exported;
- a UTF-16 file is refused.

payload.title: Record and publish the recipe of every run; usable from a challenges repo
payload.body:
## What this does

Makes `mjlab-microduck` usable as the base of another repo (the upcoming `microduck-challenges`, one folder per Microduck Arena challenge), and makes every published policy carry the recipe that trained it. **Every change is additive**: `train`, `play`, `publish --onnx`, `publish --task … --wandb-run-path`, `scripts/export.py`, `scripts/infer_policy.py`, `scripts/hf/train_hf.py` and `train … --hf-jobs` keep their flags, behaviour and outputs.

### Record what trained a run
- `train` now writes `provenance.json` in the run's log directory when the runner starts: exact command, seed, task, the checkout's `repo` (origin URL, credentials stripped), `commit`, `branch`, `dirty` (untracked files count), the installed `mjlab-microduck` version/commit, start time. It describes the git checkout `train` runs in, not the library's own path.
- Written once: `play`/`export` building a runner on an existing run never overwrite it.
- HF Jobs: the job receives the submitter's checkout (the tarball has no `.git`), and the uploader also pushes `provenance.json`, so a cloud run is as reproducible as a local one.

### Publish a run in one argument
- `publish --run <log dir> [--checkpoint N]`: picks the last (or the given) checkpoint, exports it, publishes it, and uploads the `.pt` as `checkpoint.pt` next to `policy.onnx`.
- The manifest's `training` block gains `command`, `seed`, `base`, `started` (all existing keys kept). The model card ends with a *Reproduce* block (clone, checkout, `uv run train …`), omitted when no commit is known.
- A `dirty` run is refused unless `--allow-dirty`. Only on the `--run` path; the other paths behave as before.
- When the recorded repo is the upstream of the cwd's fork, the run is attributed to the fork.
- The manifest now says what the robot wears: `robot.accessories` (e.g. `["roller_blades"]`), read from the model's mesh files. `validate_manifest` refuses an unknown accessory; a legacy manifest without the key stays valid.

### Challenges
- New `mjlab_microduck.challenge`: a challenge's `tasks.py` calls `challenge.register(__file__)` to register the `challenge.toml` beside it (event, task, kind, recipe); `env.py` reads its exposed knobs with `challenge.params(__file__)`. `publish` then finds the event and kind from the task id, so `--repo` is enough.

### Tools usable from another repo
- `microduck <command>` (`train | play | list-envs | export | publish | check | infer`) delegates to the existing entry points, with `argv[0]` rewritten so the `--hf-jobs` and provenance hooks still fire. `microduck check` runs publish's verifications without the Hub.
- `scripts/hf/uploader.py` → `mjlab_microduck.hf_uploader`, `scripts/infer_policy.py` → `mjlab_microduck.infer` (declared as the `infer` script). The old scripts stay as shims. The HF Jobs bootstrap calls modules, so it works from a repo that doesn't have these scripts.
- README: a section on using this package from another repo.

### Publish and enter in one command (for the Arena's workshop)
- `publish --enter [--arena <url>]` enters the new revision on the Microduck Arena right after the upload, with the user's Hugging Face token (`Authorization: Bearer`), and prints the entry's official time and page. Without `--enter`, `publish` behaves as before.
- It exits 3, instead of crashing, when the Arena hangs up or answers something that is not an entry, and it never follows a redirect with the token.
- A new repo that would be created private is refused before it is created: the Arena cannot read a private entry.
- HF Jobs: the run's TensorBoard files are uploaded with its checkpoints, and the automatic export reads the run's own checkpoint path.

## How to test

```bash
uv sync
uv run --with pytest pytest tests -q        # CPU only, no GPU or network needed
```

By hand: `uv run train <task> …` then `uv run publish --run logs/rsl_rl/<exp>/<run> --repo <you>/<name> --dry-run`.

## Context

Design: the "challenge workshop" spec in `pollen-robotics/microduck-arena` (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-24-challenge-workshop-design.md`). Draft because `microduck-challenges` will depend on this branch until it merges.

payload.title: BallKick: PPO can converge to "kick then collapse" at ~40-57° tilt, under the 70° fell_over threshold
payload.body:
Hi, thanks for open-sourcing microduck_rl, it's been great to learn from.

While training `Mjlab-BallKick-Flat-MicroDuck` on a laptop GPU I kept getting a PPO policy that kicks hard and then falls onto its back for the rest of the episode. Because it settles at roughly 40-57° of trunk tilt, the `fell_over` termination (`bad_orientation`, 70°) never fires, so the episode runs to time-out and the policy keeps most of the kick reward. Sharing in case it's useful; it may well be a known trade-off.

**Setup**
- repo at `cb70b79` (develop, 2026-09-14), no code changes (the run's saved git diff is empty)
- `uv run train Mjlab-BallKick-Flat-MicroDuck` with `--env.scene.num-envs 1024` (and one run at 2048), default agent config otherwise, right foot
- evaluation: exported ONNX, deterministic actions, 512 episodes, push curriculum held at stage 0; tilt measured the same way as `bad_orientation` (acos of projected gravity z)

**What I see**

| run | peak ball speed | trunk tilt at episode end | episodes ending upright (<30°) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| PPO 1024 envs, seed 42, 1500 iters | 1.47 m/s | 57° | 0% |
| PPO 1024 envs, seeds 42/43/44, 300 iters | 1.47-1.60 m/s | 40-47° | 0% (3/3 seeds) |
| PPO 2048 envs, seed 42, 300 iters | 1.41 m/s | 36° | 0% |
| released `ball_kick_right.onnx` (microduck-policies) | 1.34 m/s | 1° | 100% |

In the 1500-iteration run the policy is already collapsing at iteration 100 and never recovers; the return keeps rising while the final lean gets worse. The training logs show it too: `Episode_Reward/upright` sits around 0.1 (weight 2.0) while `ball_forward_velocity` is ~11. It's also visible in `uv run play`.

**What I couldn't test:** the recommended 4096 envs (doesn't fit on my 6 GB GPU) or a run as long as the released policy's. So this may only show up at smaller batch sizes, which your released policy suggests.

**Possible fixes**, if it's worth closing:
- a lower `fell_over` limit for this task (something like 40-45°; the policies that stay up end at 1-3° of tilt, though I haven't measured the peak lean during the swing, so the right value needs checking), or
- a trunk-height termination (e.g. `root_height_below_minimum`), or
- gating/scaling the kick reward by uprightness after contact.

For comparison, an off-policy run (FastSAC, same env, 1024 envs) kicked at 1.40 m/s and stayed upright in 2 of 3 seeds, so the task is clearly learnable at this scale. Scripts, logs and videos are here if you want to reproduce: https://github.com/Rishitha2628/microduck-kick (see `docs/experiments.md`).

Happy to open a PR for whichever option you'd prefer.

payload.title: `head_camera` <camera> element points backwards into the head
payload.body:
The `<camera name="head_camera">` in `src/mjlab_microduck/robot/microduck/robot_allcollisions.xml`
(line 313 on develop at 08680d3, also in the other robot_*.xml variants) has `quat="0 0 -1 0"`. MuJoCo cameras
look along their own -Z, so at the reset pose it looks backwards into the head shell and renders a grey
image. Nothing in this repo renders from it, so training is unaffected; anyone rendering from the head
camera hits it.

Evidence:
- The runtime already knows the right frame: the `head_camera` site (line 312) composed with
  `SITE_TO_CV2` from microduck's `kinematics/src/head.rs` gives, in MuJoCo camera convention,
  look = -Z and up = +X in the head body frame. The `<camera>` element gives look = +Z, up = +Y..
- Setting the camera quat to `0.7071068 0 0 -0.7071068` matches that frame exactly; the rendered
  frame then shows the floor and horizon ahead.
- PRs #21 and #22 each overwrite `cam_quat` at load time to work around this (#22's README and
  `test_head_camera_optical_correction_...` describe it), and so does
  https://github.com/mshooter/microduck_academy (`smoke.py`, `CAMERA_QUAT_FORWARD`).

Two questions before a PR:
1. Is the file generated from a CAD export? If so the fix belongs in the export step.
2. The physical camera is mounted a quarter turn off and mediad leaves rotation to the consumer.
   Should the sim camera be upright (as above) or match the raw sensor?

Happy to send the one-line PR once you say which.

payload.title: Rough terrain: generator runs in random mode, and play cfgs mutate the shared terrain config used for training
payload.body:
Hi, thanks for microduck_rl. While training the rough velocity tasks (`Mjlab-Velocity-Rough-MicroDuck`, `Mjlab-VelStand-Rough-MicroDuck`) on an RTX 5090 I found two things in the terrain setup that change what the terrain curriculum does. Both are still present on `main` (cfe1c2a).

**1. `MICRODUCK_ROUGH_TERRAINS_CFG` runs in random mode, so terrain levels are not a difficulty ladder**

`MICRODUCK_ROUGH_TERRAINS_CFG` (`microduck_velocity_env_cfg.py`, line 127) does not set `curriculum`, and mjlab's `TerrainGeneratorCfg.curriculum` defaults to `False`. In random mode every patch samples a random sub-terrain and a random difficulty (`difficulty = self.np_rng.uniform(*self.cfg.difficulty_range)` in `mjlab/terrains/terrain_generator.py`), so rows are not ordered by difficulty. The `terrain_levels` curriculum then moves robots between rows of randomly rough patches, and `Curriculum/terrain_levels/mean` does not track terrain difficulty. mjlab's own rough velocity tasks turn curriculum mode on explicitly (`tasks/velocity/config/g1/env_cfgs.py` and `go1/env_cfgs.py`: `cfg.scene.terrain.terrain_generator.curriculum = True`).

**2. The play branch mutates the shared module-level config, which the training cfg also uses**

Each rough `make_*_env_cfg` assigns the module-level object directly (`cfg.scene.terrain.terrain_generator = MICRODUCK_ROUGH_TERRAINS_CFG`), and its `if play:` branch then sets `curriculum = False`, `num_cols = 5`, `num_rows = 5` on that same object. Task registration builds the play cfgs too, so after `import mjlab_microduck.tasks` the training cfgs point at a 5 x 5 grid instead of the configured 10 x 20. Affected sites on `main`: `microduck_velocity_env_cfg.py` 753/772-774, `microduck_sitstand_env_cfg.py` 746-750, `microduck_standup_env_cfg.py` 842-846, `microduck_ground_pick_env_cfg.py` 608-612.

Repro (no GPU needed):

```python
import mjlab_microduck.tasks  # registers tasks, builds play cfgs
from mjlab_microduck.tasks import microduck_velstand_env_cfg as vs, microduck_velocity_env_cfg as vc

train = vs.make_microduck_velstand_env_cfg(rough=True).scene.terrain.terrain_generator
play = vs.make_microduck_velstand_env_cfg(play=True, rough=True).scene.terrain.terrain_generator
print(train.curriculum, train.num_rows, train.num_cols)  # False 5 5  (configured: rows 10, cols 20)
print(train is vc.MICRODUCK_ROUGH_TERRAINS_CFG, train is play)  # True True
```

The dumped `params/env.yaml` of three of my rough training runs agrees: `curriculum: false`, `num_rows: 5`, `num_cols: 5`.

**Possible fix**

What I am testing locally on the velocity family: `deepcopy` the generator in each `make_*_env_cfg` (the module already imports `deepcopy`), and set `curriculum = True` for training while play keeps its 5 x 5 random grid on its own copy:

```python
cfg.scene.terrain.terrain_generator = deepcopy(MICRODUCK_ROUGH_TERRAINS_CFG)
cfg.scene.terrain.terrain_generator.curriculum = not play
```

With that change, a 200-iteration run of `Mjlab-VelStand-Rough-MicroDuck` from the same checkpoint (4096 envs) dumps `curriculum: true`, `num_rows: 10`, and the terrain curriculum climbs: mean level 3.07 in the first 50 iterations to 4.43 in the last 50, with robots reaching row 9 after about 100 iterations. Without it, the same start stayed on a 5 x 5 grid with max level 4. (These runs use a tracking-based promote/demote rule in my fork rather than the stock distance rule, so the exact numbers will differ on `main`.)

I have not changed SitStand, StandUp or GroundPick rough locally, since restoring their 10 x 20 grid changes their training and I have not measured it. Happy to open a PR if that is useful.

payload.title: Fix wandb credential lookup on Windows (~/_netrc, not ~/.netrc)
payload.body:
## Summary
- `_wandb_api_key()` in `hf_jobs.py` only checked `~/.netrc` for cached wandb credentials
- On Windows, `wandb login` writes credentials to `~/_netrc` instead — Python's `netrc` module doesn't check that filename automatically
- As a result, `--hf-jobs` reported `"no API key found"` on Windows even right after a successful `wandb login`

## Fix
Check both `~/.netrc` and `~/_netrc`, falling back gracefully if either is missing.

## Test plan
- [x] Ran `wandb login` on Windows, confirmed `~/_netrc` was written (not `~/.netrc`)
- [x] Before fix: `--hf-jobs` failed with "no API key found"
- [x] After fix: submitted a real HF Jobs smoke test (`Mjlab-Velocity-Flat-MicroDuck`, 5 iterations); wandb API key forwarded correctly and the run appeared in the wandb dashboard

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

payload.title: fix(hf-jobs): auto-export never finds the checkpoint
payload.body:
The auto-export step at the end of a HF Jobs run never fires: it reports
`[bootstrap] no checkpoint found, skipping auto-export` even though the uploader
has just pushed several `model_*.pt` files from the very same run.

Two bugs, one behind the other:

1. **The glob is one level too shallow.** `rsl_rl` writes to
   `logs/rsl_rl/<experiment_name>/<timestamp>_<run_name>/model_*.pt`, but the
   bootstrap looks for `logs/rsl_rl/*/model_*.pt`, which matches nothing.

2. **The checkpoint is passed by basename.** `scripts/export.py` does
   `Path(cfg.checkpoint_file)` and then `.exists()`, resolved relative to the
   working directory (`/work`), so a bare `model_19.pt` fails even once found.

This matters more than a missing convenience: `scripts/export.py` builds an mjlab
env and therefore needs CUDA. A user with no local GPU — the exact audience
`--hf-jobs` exists for — cannot export the checkpoint afterwards. The run
completes, uploads its `.pt` files, and leaves nothing deployable behind.

Verified on two jobs, `Mjlab-Velocity-Flat-MicroDuck`, 1024 envs, 20 iterations,
flavor `l4x1`:

- before: `[bootstrap] no checkpoint found, skipping auto-export`
- after: `[bootstrap] auto-exporting ONNX from model_19.pt` → `Written /work/policy.onnx` → `[bootstrap] uploaded exported/policy.onnx`

payload.title: Add play-dead task: stand, flop onto the back, and hold
payload.body:
## Why

Sit is a polite sit. Roulade lands on its feet. Standup starts already down. Nothing in the pad means **die and stay dead** — swap the ONNX in, the duck goes down and holds; swap sitstand/standup to revive.

Play-dead is **supine** (belly up, −90° pitch), not “inverted”. `upright_cos = −1` is a headstand **and** a face-plant; a policy will farm whichever is cheaper. The orientation signal is world-z of body +X (`body_supine_cos_from_quat`). Height rewards are gated on `supine_cos > 0` so sitting (`z ≈ 0.060`) cannot collect the dead-height peak.

## What

- New env family `Mjlab-PlayDead-{Flat,Rough}-MicroDuck` (+ backlash twins on the allcollisions model)
- 61D actor obs: 48 proprio + twist(3) + head(4) pad + body(6) pad — hot-swappable with walk/stand/roulade
- Reset mix: 75% standing (learn the flop) / 25% already face-up (learn the hold); reverse curriculum raises the dead fraction; face-down stays at 0
- `scripts/infer_policy.py --playdead` (key **D**). Default is hold-until-D-again — play-dead does not end standing
- CPU cfg tests lock the contract, signs, sit-basin audit, and registration

## AGENTS.md bar

```bash
uv run --with pytest pytest tests/test_playdead_cfg.py
uv run train Mjlab-PlayDead-Flat-MicroDuck --env.scene.num-envs 64 --agent.max_iterations 5
```

Ran on a Spark (GB10): 16 play-dead tests + full CPU suite (171) green. Smoke 64 envs × 5 iters: actor obs **(61,)**, every reward term computed, `Episode_Termination/nan_state = 0`, self-negating penalties logged **≤ 0**, ONNX export **61 → 14**.

This is the env, not a converged policy. A real run is `~1000–2000` iters at 4096 envs (`experiment_name=microduck_playdead`), then `scripts/export.py` (bakes the normalizer — mandatory).

## Deploy rehearsal

```bash
uv run scripts/infer_policy.py --walking walk.onnx --standing stand.onnx \
    --playdead playdead.onnx --new-cmd-obs
```

`D` plays dead and holds; `D` again hands back. Revive with standup/sitstand, not walk.

payload.title: fix: keep CPU policy replay compatible with an independent mouth actuator
payload.body:
Adding an independent mouth actuator makes CPU replay treat it as a fifteenth policy joint, causing a `(15,)` / `(14,)` broadcast error with the released walking policy.

This maps the fourteen policy joints by name and gives the mouth a separate `set_mouth_target()` / `--mouth-target RADIANS` path. Existing 51D/61D layouts stay unchanged. XML position actuators with native `timeconst` filtering remain supported. No stock beak model or grasping behavior is added. Related to #27.

[Reproduction commands and pinned policy](https://github.com/payals/microduck_rl/blob/fix/independent-mouth-inference/docs/independent-mouth-replay.md) · [recorded before/after output](https://github.com/payals/microduck_rl/blob/fix/independent-mouth-inference/docs/mouth-replay-results.json). The headless reproducer uses only the old API: the stock scene runs in both versions; adding the synthetic actuator fails before the fix and runs after it.

Validation:

- 26 mouth/replay tests pass, covering both actuator paths, legacy/current observations, target isolation, ordering, delays and filtered position actuators.
- Full CPU suite: 251 passed, one existing GPU-specific skip, **in the local environment with Torch 2.13, Warp 1.14 and patched mjlab**. This is not a pristine upstream CUDA-environment result. The standalone reproduction uses MuJoCo 3.10.0 and ONNX Runtime 1.24.4 without Torch/mjlab.

payload.title: Feature/outdoor terrain
feat: `--modal` — train on Modal GPUs, sibling of the HF Jobs path
payload.body:
Adds a Modal backend for training, alongside the existing HF Jobs path. Same
contract as `--hf-jobs` — same source snapshot (tracked + uncommitted files),
same wandb forwarding, same auto-export to ONNX — but the dependency install is
baked into a cached image, so a warm start is seconds instead of minutes.

## Usage

Your normal train command, plus `--modal`:

```bash
uv run train Mjlab-Velocity-Flat-MicroDuck \
    --env.scene.num-envs 4096 --agent.max_iterations 6000 --modal
```

Without the flag, nothing changes. Submission flags (`--gpu`, `--timeout`,
`--detach`, `--dry-run`, `--no-wandb`, `--no-export`, …) are consumed locally;
everything else is forwarded verbatim to `uv run train` in the container.
`scripts/modal/README.md` has the full set.

## How it works

`train_hook.py` previously hardcoded the one `--hf-jobs` flag. It now dispatches
a table, still intercepted from the `mjlab.tasks` plugin entry point before tyro
parses argv:

```
--hf-jobs  -> mjlab_microduck.hf_jobs
--modal    -> mjlab_microduck.modal_jobs
```

Each submitter module exposes `submit(argv) -> int` and receives argv minus the
flag, so adding a third backend is a table entry. `scripts/modal/train_modal.py`
is a shim that calls `submit()` directly, matching the HF path's escape hatch.

Image is `nvidia/cuda:12.4.1-cudnn-runtime-ubuntu22.04` + python 3.12 + uv, with
`uv sync --frozen --no-dev --no-install-project` cached until `pyproject.toml` /
`uv.lock` change. A Modal Volume `microduck-rl-logs` is mounted at `/work/logs`
and committed every 60 s, so checkpoints survive a timeout or a crash. The wandb
key travels as a per-run Secret (read from `$WANDB_API_KEY` or `~/.netrc`), so it
is not baked into the image.

## Notes

- Log/stop hints print the Modal **app id**, not the app name: training apps are
  ephemeral, and `modal app logs <name>` resolves names only for *deployed* apps
  (it errors with "No App with name ... found"). `scripts/modal/README.md` says
  the same.
- `modal>=1.0` is in a `[dependency-groups] dev` group, so it is not pulled into
  the container (`uv sync --no-dev`).

## Testing

`tests/test_modal_jobs.py` (8 tests) covers flag interception, argv forwarding,
and the submission spec; `tests/test_hf_jobs_flag.py` still passes unchanged, so
the refactor doesn't disturb the HF path. 20 passed locally.

End to end: a 6000-iteration `Mjlab-Velocity-Flat-MicroDuck` run at 4096 envs on
an L4 finished in 5h09m, exit 0, mean reward 119.4, with checkpoints in wandb and
`exported/policy.onnx` written to the volume.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

payload.title: Policy export contract
payload.body:
Adds `docs/export-contract.md`, which states what an exported `.onnx` is: graph, 61-D observation layout, action, joint order, home pose, actuator gain and rate.

The goal is one source of truth between training and the robot. Today the daemon hardcodes the same facts (home pose, `kp` 200, joint order) and nothing checks that they still match what a policy was trained against. mjlab's generic metadata can't do that job either: under BAM, `joint_stiffness` exports 1.0.

The contract adds a `microduck` JSON metadata key, filled from the training env at export time. The daemon will read it at load: it refuses a policy whose value is present and wrong, and uses `kp_fw`/`action_scale` unless the robot's config overrides them.

This PR is the doc only, and nothing writes the key yet. The exporter change will land here before merging, followed by the daemon reader in pollen-robotics/microduck.

cc. @Drenayaz @nicolas-rabault @apirrone - More of a starting point than something formalized but what do you think?

payload.title: Velocity-family training converges to standing-in-place across all reward/curriculum variants — full diagnostic matrix
payload.body:
**Title: Velocity-family training converges to standing-in-place across all reward/curriculum variants — full diagnostic matrix**

## Environment

- Repo at `29e887e` (Sep 2, includes `fix not walking` + the velocity2 merge)
- Pinned env from `uv.lock`: warp-lang 1.12.0, mujoco 3.10.0, mjlab 1.3.0, torch 2.9.1+cu128
- 4× L4 (sm_89), driver 570.172.08 (CUDA 12.8), Ubuntu, training on 4096 envs
- Tasks: `Mjlab-Velocity-Flat-MicroDuck`, `Mjlab-VelStand-Flat-MicroDuck`, plus a registered RampReg variant of Velocity-Flat (see below)

## Symptom

Every velocity-family run converges to a **standing / stepping-in-place policy**:

- `Metrics/twist/error_vel_xy` plateaus at ~0.43 (command ranges lin ±0.4 / ang ±1.0, so ≈ mean |cmd|)
- Net displacement 0.1–0.6 m per 20 s episode; `Episode_Reward/air_time ≈ 0.002` (feet never leave the ground) until very late
- Reward breakdown shows `upright` (2.0) and `head_pose_tracking` (2.0) as the dominant positive mass while the robot stands

Meanwhile the **pose tasks train fine** with the same pipeline: StandUp-Flat reaches 90% envs standing within 200 steps; SitStand transitions verified (98% of envs switch posture). So the env/RL plumbing itself works.

## Diagnostic matrix (what we tried)

| # | Hypothesis | Experiment | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Regularizers suppress gait exploration (AGENTS.md "attempt-tax") | Tracking-only rewards (all 11 non-tracking terms weight 0), 1500 iters | error 0.39→0.23, slow but real; still no gait; displacement <1 m |
| 2 | Same + regularizers ramped in at iter 800 (repo's `reward_weight`) | RampReg run, 5000 iters | error dips to 0.15 @1565 then rises to 0.37 — standing wins again |
| 3 | Gait bootstrap missing | air_time (3.0) + foot_swing + foot_clearance at full weight from step 0, all penalties deferred to iter 6000 | error briefly 0.10, air_time activates (0.02), late-episode displacement surge to 0.52 m — then regresses to standing by iter 11300 |
| 4 | Torque insufficiency (BAM M6 force_limit ±1.07 Nm) | vin_range (6.5,8.2)→(6.5,16.4) (force_limit ≈ ×2 via kt·V/R), tracking-only 300 iters | error 0.44 @242 vs 0.29 control — **worse**, hypothesis rejected |
| 5 | DR push_robot events corrupt displacement evals | Disabled push_robot; forced constant forward command via `obs["actor"][48:51]=(0.3,0,0)` | displacement 0.04 m / path 0.11 m over 12 s — policy genuinely does not walk |
| 6 | Official checkpoint as reference | `alpha_walking.onnx` under our sim (privileged obs) | drifts 0.66 m / 20 s — also does not walk (obs-convention mismatch suspected: sensor-view vs privileged, so inconclusive) |
| 7 | Version drift | `uv.lock`-pinned install, verified | ruled out |

Note on #5/#6: we found `push_robot` interval events (3–6 s) firing during train-mode evals — worth flagging for anyone benchmarking displacement on train-mode envs.

## Ask

Our working hypothesis is now that something differs between the HF Jobs training setup and a stock `uv.lock` local run, or that a specific seed/config detail is needed to escape the standing local optimum. Questions:

1. Has anyone hit standing-in-place convergence on the velocity tasks, and what was the escape?
2. Is there a known-good wandb run config (seed, hyperparameters, any uncommitted tweaks) for the merged velocity recipe that we should replicate exactly?
3. For `alpha_walking.onnx`: what observation view does it expect (privileged sim obs vs onboard sensor view), and what normalizer stats/ordering? (Related to #40.)

Happy to share training logs, checkpoints, the RampReg task patch, and the diagnostic scripts (`eval_skill.py`, `disp_eval.py`, `force_cmd_eval.py`).

## What works

StandUp / SitStand / (partially) VelStand-prone-reset recovery — all verified numerically with train-mode evals. The pipeline, DR stack, and eval tooling are solid; it's specifically velocity-gait discovery that never happens.

payload.title: How is the articulated beak/grasp modeled in simulation?
payload.body:
Hi! I’m looking into grasping with MicroDuck and wanted to clarify how the beak is intended to be modeled in simulation.

From the current public microduck_rl model and policy interface, I understand that the locomotion policies use 14 actuated joints and that the mouth is excluded from the policy action space. The current GroundPick behavior also appears to focus on lowering the mouth tip to the ground and returning upright, rather than simulating an articulated beak closing on an object.

A few questions:

Is there currently a physical jaw/beak joint + actuator model used internally for grasp simulation that is not yet included in this repository?
On the real robot, is beak closing during the advertised Grab behavior handled by a scripted/high-level controller outside the 14D policy?
Is physics-based grasping — articulated beak + contact/friction, without kinematic attachment/latching — planned for the public simulator?

If this functionality is currently missing, I’d be interested in implementing it in a backward-compatible way: keeping the existing 14D locomotion policies unchanged, adding an independently controlled jaw actuator, and providing a minimal contact-based grasp demo.

Would that be a contribution you’d be open to reviewing upstream?

payload.title: Add headstand routine training tasks
payload.body:
## Summary

Adds six simulation training tasks for a headstand routine: fold into a pike, kick up with legs together or split, switch the leading leg while inverted, and return to standing through a back roll or split-over exit. The routine combines these policies with Pollen's existing standing policy.

The tasks, rewards, handover data, and tests are self-contained; no companion checkout is needed to train or test them. The policies retain the shared 61-value observation layout, 14-joint controls, and BAM actuators.

## What changed

- `microduck_headstand_env_cfg.py` and `microduck_backroll_env_cfg.py`: task configurations; `tasks/__init__.py`: task registration.
- `tasks/mdp.py`: rewards and starting-state curricula.
- `tasks/handover_pike_from_fold.npz`: 512 recorded fold handovers, checked against the robot XML hash; `scripts/headstand/collect_handover.py`: collector.
- `tests/test_headstand_cfg.py`: CPU regression tests; `.gitignore`: includes the handover data file in version control.
- [Headstand README](https://github.com/zachgarner/microduck_rl/blob/29ed59c08d1253b6e898330acbb105b8eab0cabc/docs/headstand/README.md): routine, training settings, evaluation criteria, and results.

All 512 handovers are retained to preserve the evaluated checkpoints' training data. A CPU pose-contact audit found 511 with head and both feet touching, and one with head and one foot. The current collector requires both feet; the audit does not replay the original Warp contact history.

## Test plan

- [x] `WANDB_MODE=offline uv run list-envs`: all six headstand tasks listed.
- [x] `uv run --with pytest pytest tests/ -q`: **272 passed, 1 skipped**.
- [x] Five-iteration CPU smoke test, 64 environments, no NaN terminations:

  ```bash
  WANDB_MODE=offline uv run train Mjlab-HeadstandFold-Flat-MicroDuck \
    --gpu-ids None --env.scene.num-envs 64 --agent.max_iterations 5
  ```

- [x] Optional companion evaluator and training CLI checks: **8 passed** (`uv run --with pytest pytest ../tools/test_evaluation.py ../tools/test_training_cli.py -q` from its training submodule).
- [x] Anonymous downloads verified for all six published packages; the download helper also passed with an empty destination and on a repeat run.
- [x] Saved checkpoint evaluations: `uv run ../tools/run_verification.py --routine-seeds 0 1 2 --individual --workers 2` from the companion's training submodule.

Full routine: **87/96**, seeds 0/1/2: **28/32, 29/32, 30/32**, no automatic resets; median successful completion **12.3 s**. Each of the six individual policies: **32/32 at seed 0**.
The optional [videos, evaluation scripts, raw logs, and training jobs](https://github.com/zachgarner/microduck-headstand/tree/a5dad724d124fe50eee9f78942361bb794950ff2) include reports in `results/verified/` with checkpoint and evaluator-source hashes and per-attempt outcomes. The six original checkpoints and normalized ONNX exports are now public on Hugging Face under `ZachGarner`. Run `uv run ../tools/download_policies.py` in the companion training checkout to fetch the checkpoints and standing policy at pinned revisions with hash verification; no W&B or Hugging Face login is required. The reported rollout counts use the original checkpoints; the ONNX exports passed shape and output smoke checks.

Success requires every held stage, the specified leg shape during headstand holds, and standing on both feet at the final frame. All results are from simulation; this has not been tested on hardware. Head-force measurements are sampled at 50 Hz and can miss shorter impacts. Individual exit checks establish final standing, not leg shape throughout the exit. The latest routine demonstration is v16; its video is separate from the seeded evaluation reports. Earlier recordings are retained as history.

payload.title: velstand: hand fast-rotating fallen frames to PPO, not the stand expert
payload.body:
## Why 
[Open item (a) in the VelStand cfg docstring](https://github.com/pollen-robotics/microduck_rl/blob/cb70b792312d559a4da09064d92009079671815f/src/mjlab_microduck/tasks/microduck_velstand_env_cfg.py#L112-L115) : convulsions rising from the back after a real fall: during simulations, face-up landings after a push recover 58–77 % while face-up spawns recover ~100 %, and the stand expert has the same hole. The lever turns out to be the cloning mask, not a reward. The mask is tilt-only: every frame above 35° is regressed onto an expert that was trained from HOME-pose spawns and has never seen the leg states a real fall leaves behind, and because the BC pass runs after PPO, whatever PPO learns on those frames is undone each iteration. That is the teacher ceiling runs 5–6 hit.

## What changes (in `distill.py`) 
A fallen frame is cloned only while `|base_ang_vel| < 3 rad/s` (obs slice `[0:3]`). Frames that are still rotating belong to PPO and the recovery rewards you already have; the expert teaches the get-up once the body has settled. Natural MicroDuck tumbles run 3.5–5.5 rad/s and a slow push-up stays well under 3, so the split is clean. Cloned fallen fraction 0.25 → 0.06; the excluded share is logged as `Loss/expert_bc_dynamic_ppo_frac`. Threshold and slice are `bc_cfg` entries with defaults in `distill.py`; the `ENABLE_*` toggle + constant in the cfg with a cfg test, per AGENTS.md, is ready on `velstand/dynamic-fall-cfg-toggle-v2` if you prefer it in the same PR. @apirrone - happy to adjust! 

## Measured
Warm start from the published VelStand policy (run 4 actor rebuilt from the Hub ONNX, fresh critic re-fitted 50 iterations), 4096 envs, every curriculum pinned at its final stage (pushes ±1.2 m/s, prone spawns 45 %, tax and bounty on), same seeds for baseline and change, scalars averaged over the last 100 iterations. "Fell" = was upright earlier in the episode. Ranges are min–max over seeds.

| task, length, seeds | fell face-up recovered | fell side recovered | time to up, face-up | `fallen_too_long` / episode |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Flat, 600 it, 10 seeds | 0.77–0.79 → **0.88–0.92** | 0.87–0.88 → 0.92–0.94 | 2.4–2.6 → 1.6–1.9 s | 0.45–0.53 → 0.09–0.16 |
| Flat, 4000 it, 3 seeds | 0.78–0.79 → **0.92–0.94** | 0.88 → 0.94–0.95 | 2.5 → 1.5–1.7 s | 0.41–0.47 → 0.05–0.08 |
| Rough-Backlash, 600 it, 3 seeds | 0.74–0.76 → **0.85–0.86** | 0.85–0.86 → 0.88–0.90 | 2.5 → 1.8–1.9 s | 0.57–0.67 → 0.24–0.36 |

No seed overlap on any recovery metric at any length, and the gap widens with training. Face-down recovery, `servo_stall`, and head / trunk / servo impact peaks are unchanged (head ~40 N flat, ~32 N rough). Walking itself, measured without pushes, is unchanged:

| length, seeds | baseline | this change |
|---|---|---|
| 600 it, seeds 45 / 46 / 47 | 0.176 / 0.173 / 0.178 | 0.176 / 0.178 / 0.182 |
| 2000 it, seeds 42 / 43 / 44 | 0.179 / 0.185 / 0.175 | 0.198 / 0.171 / 0.178 |

Video: seed 42 at 2000 it, free play with topple pushes, baseline left, this change right.

payload.title: Cross-stack reward parity: feet_flat sign fix, PR gate, MJX migration scaffold
payload.body:
## What this is

Four commits that make the CPU stack (`microduck-lab`) and this MJLab/MJX stack
agree on reward semantics, and turn that agreement into a CI-enforced gate.

Submitted from a fork (`hzzqq/microduck_rl`) — I have no write access to the
upstream repo.

## 1. `f0a1b07` — Fix `feet_flat_penalty`: the foot site's local Z is not world-up

**This is a real defect, not a refactor.** The reward assumed the foot site's
local Z points world-up. In `robot_allcollisions.xml` the foot sites carry
`quat="0 0 0.707107 0.707107"` (rolled 90 degrees), so at rest the local Z is
world **+Y**. A perfectly flat foot therefore scored the penalty's
**theoretical maximum** — the term was inverted: the cheapest way to score 0 was
to stand on a knife edge, exactly what the term exists to prevent.

Fix: read the reference off the model (`_foot_rest_gravity_ref`, cached on the
env) and penalize squared distance from it — which is what the CPU stack's
`foot_flat_ref` has always done. Measured at the STAND keyframe:

- CPU `_flat_feet` -> `1.000000` (1.0 == perfectly flat)
- MJLab rule (old) -> `0.999999` (0.0 == perfectly flat == full penalty)

Six configs are affected: `jump`, `spin`, `ground_pick`, `roller_crouch`,
`roller_slope`, `velocity_rollers`. Their existing performance numbers were
produced under the wrong sign and should be re-baselined on GPU.

We deliberately did **not** re-tune weights — that needs training data, not
static analysis.

## 2. `5a3a0f5` — Reusable reward parity gate (CI backstop)

`reward_parity_gate.py` turns "you forgot a cross-stack parity test" into a red
CI instead of a postmortem. It AST-scans `mdp.py` for functions that project
world gravity into a site/geom frame (`gravity_vec_w` + `quat_apply_inverse`)
and fails on any that is not registered.

The registry is split into `REWARD_TERMS` (parity-required) and
`FRAME_HELPERS` (the self-calibrating `_foot_rest_gravity_ref`), so the gate
does not false-positive on the fix itself. Docstrings are stripped before
scanning — the old formula is quoted in the `feet_flat` docstring, which
otherwise produces a false hit (this bit me twice).

## 3. `b437851` — Jump task `-Backlash` variant + first-run checklist

Registers `Mjlab-Jump-Flat-Backlash-MicroDuck` using the **walk** robot (the
jump task is a flat walk-model task; using `allcollisions` would silently swap
the collision model). Adds `scripts/jump_first_run.py`, a runnable first-boot
checklist for a CUDA host: GPU stack visible, cfg constructible in both train
and play modes, variant registered, short rollout shows phase signal.

Important: the script deliberately does **not** use total reward as the pass
criterion — squat-and-rise scores as well as a real jump on the crouch/launch
terms. It reports the phase terms (`jump_airborne` / `jump_apex`) and tells you
to confirm they have signal before committing to long training.

## 4. `7fefa94` — MJX parity-first migration scaffold (execution BLOCKED)

`mjx_parity_migration.py`: `build_migration_plan()` enumerates every term
needing CPU<->MJX numeric parity, read from the gate registry so it cannot
drift from CI. `execute_migration()` is the real alignment loop and returns
`{"status": "BLOCKED"}` without `mujoco_warp`/CUDA — a machine-assertable
block, not a silent no-op. `BLOCKED_DIRECTIONS.md` documents what unblocks it.

## Testing

- `tests/test_reward_parity.py` — 4 tests; **verified red when the fix is reverted**.
- `tests/test_reward_parity_gate.py` — 5 tests.
- `tests/test_mjx_parity_migration.py` — 2 tests.

All green locally. The MJLab-dependent tests cannot be collected in my
environment (no `mjlab` / `mujoco_warp` / CUDA), so this branch still needs a
GPU run before merge.

## What we need from maintainers

1. A CUDA run of `scripts/jump_first_run.py` and
   `mjx_parity_migration.execute_migration(env_factory)`.
2. A decision on re-baselining the 6 configs affected by the `feet_flat` sign bug.

payload.title: Approach-and-inspect task (Mjlab-ApproachInspect-*-MicroDuck)
payload.body:
## What

A new task family: the duck walks to a small static target, stops on a 22 cm standoff ring, aims its head at it, holds the look for 2 s, then turns away. Built on `make_microduck_velocity_env_cfg` so every DR / sim2real block is the velocity recipe verbatim (locked by tests), obs stays 61-D and actions 14 so the policy hot-swaps with the walking policy.

- `tasks/approach_inspect_mdp.py` — reward terms in their own module (no `mdp.py` edits): potential-based ring progress (Δ of −|d − standoff|), head-aim Gaussian gated on the ring, L1 on a 1 s EMA of bearing error, a slewed dwell latch (rate-limited, cannot be jackpotted by arriving fast, does not accumulate while moving), a ring-gated planar-speed penalty, and potential-based turn-away. Self-negating penalties take positive weights per AGENTS.md.
- `TargetCommand` writes `[dx_norm, dy_norm, phase_flag]` into the twist slot (target offset in the base yaw frame, ±1 at 1.5 m); head/body slots keep tiny sampling ranges at weight 0.
- `robot/microduck/target.xml` + `MICRODUCK_TARGET_CFG`: a fixed-base puck that mjlab auto-wraps in mocap; `reset_target_around_robot` spawns it at radius 0.4–1.5 m, any bearing.
- Gait terms (`air_time`, foot clearance/swing/slip, walking pose std) are gated on the command norm so they are active only outside the ring (d > 0.30 m); inside, the standing pose std applies.
- Registered: `Mjlab-ApproachInspect-Flat-MicroDuck`, `-Rough-`, and `-Flat-Backlash-` (walk backlash model, like Velocity).

## Verified

- `tests/test_approach_inspect_mdp.py` (11) and `tests/test_approach_inspect_cfg.py` (9) pass on CPU; the cfg tests assert every DR/obs-noise/delay term is identical to the velocity cfg and every penalty weight has the right sign.
- Env instantiates on CPU (warp cpu, 4 envs) with 61-D actor obs and 14 actions.
- 5-iteration / 64-env smoke train on CPU: all `Episode_Reward/*penalty*` ≤ 0, no NaN terminations, ONNX auto-export is `obs[1,61] → actions[1,14]`; the exported policy runs in `scripts/infer_policy.py`.
- **Not yet trained** — opened as a draft so the reward design can be read before GPU time is spent. Design notes are in the module docstrings.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

payload.title: Distill neutral-head Flamingo controller
payload.body:
## Summary

This experiment distills the published Microduck Flamingo balance actor into a
neutral-head policy while preserving its mature leg controller.

- Keeps the teacher observation normalizer and hidden layers.
- Fits only the final linear layer against fixed-head teacher rollouts using
  ridge regression.
- Constrains all four head action outputs to the neutral `HOME` target.
- Includes the ONNX policy, source dataset, distillation/evaluation scripts,
  raw telemetry, checksums, and media.

## Demo

![Animated left-foot then right-foot neutral-head Flamingo rollout](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/abhinav3/microduck_rl/refs/heads/experiment/neutral-head-flamingo/experiments/neutral_head_flamingo/media/neutral_head_left_then_right.gif)

[Download the full-quality 30-second MP4](https://github.com/abhinav3/microduck_rl/blob/experiment/neutral-head-flamingo/experiments/neutral_head_flamingo/media/neutral_head_left_then_right.mp4)

## Independent simulation result

| Measurement | Result | Acceptance |
|---|---:|---:|
| Left-foot single-support fraction | 100% | >= 95% |
| Right-foot single-support fraction | 99% | >= 95% |
| Raised right-foot median height | 9.67 cm | >= 5 cm |
| Raised left-foot median height | 7.64 cm | >= 5 cm |
| Final two-foot contact fraction | 100% | >= 95% |
| Non-foot ground-contact samples | 0 | 0 |
| Maximum trunk tilt | 27.93 deg | < 60 deg |

The command timeline holds the left-foot and right-foot poses for 10 seconds
each, with two seconds excluded from each scored window as transition time.

## Validation

- Fresh evaluation reproduced the committed metrics.
- The committed dataset reproduces the ONNX byte-for-byte with ridge `25`.
- ONNX SHA-256:
  `ca1d39539074655ad344bcf95cffb352215ba1d25b444c315cebf8a792a63e5f`
- Machine-readable results:
  [`results/summary.json`](https://github.com/abhinav3/microduck_rl/blob/experiment/neutral-head-flamingo/experiments/neutral_head_flamingo/results/summary.json)

## Provenance and limitation

The teacher is Pollen Robotics / Remi Fabre's published
[`microduck-flamingo-cycle`](https://huggingface.co/RemiFabre/microduck-flamingo-cycle)
policy and is attributed under Apache-2.0.

"Neutral head" means neutral **actuator targets**, not mechanically locked
joints. Small passive head deflection remains under load; the README reports
the measured joint ranges. This is a simulation result and does not claim
hardware validation.

payload.title: Validate simulator motor targets before updating controls
payload.body:
`Body.set_targets()` writes one actuator at a time. If conversion fails in a later slot, the handler returns an error but earlier motor targets have already changed. NaN and infinity are also accepted; even a valid JSON number such as `1e400` decodes to infinity in Python.

This validates all 15 wire targets before updating `data.ctrl`, including the mouth slot that the current model does not actuate. Targets must be a JSON array of finite numbers. Strings, booleans, nulls, nested values, and overflowing numbers are rejected. Valid targets keep the existing name-based wire mapping.

The new tests use the actual MuJoCo body model. They check unchanged controls after invalid frames, valid mapping, and a local TCP connection that receives an error and then successfully writes a valid frame. Before the fix, 31 of the first 38 cases failed.

Validation on macOS, Python 3.12, CPU:

- `uv run --with pytest pytest tests/test_body_server_targets.py -q`: 39 passed.
- `uv run --with pytest pytest tests/ -q`: 238 passed, 1 skipped.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

No GPU, policy weights, robot hardware, or credentials are required for these tests. This does not change the protocol, joint limits, actuator physics, or training configuration.

2. Normalizer statistics/source, shape and observation ordering, SHA-256, and
   an immutable link to that checkpoint and ONNX.
3. Exact exporter source repository/revision/path/digest, invocation, runtime
   versions, input checkpoint digest, and output ONNX digest.
4. Exact root MJCF repository/revision/path/digest used for training/export.
5. Exact BAM implementation and parameter repository/revision/path/digests.
6. Exact task identifier plus repository/revision/path/digest for its config.
7. Immutable evaluator implementation repository/revision/path/digest.
8. Digest-bound raw evaluation receipts naming evaluator, policy, model, BAM,
   task, cases/seeds, and output evidence digests.
9. An immutable license file/revision/digest explicitly covering the policy,
   checkpoint, normalizer, exporter, model/task inputs, and published evidence.

A signed manifest or immutable repository/model revision containing these
records is ideal. Narrative claims, mutable latest links, screenshots, videos,
or aggregate metrics without digest-bound raw evidence cannot close the gate.

payload.title: Jetson AGX Thor (JetPack 7): torch source marker cannot tell a Jetson from a GB10; SBSA wheel omits NVPL/cuDSS deps
payload.body:
## Summary

On a **Jetson AGX Thor** (JetPack 7 / L4T R38, CUDA 13.0, driver 580, `platform_machine == 'aarch64'`), `uv sync` at `29e887e` resolves torch from `download.pytorch.org/whl/cu129` because the `[tool.uv.sources]` marker only checks `sys_platform`/`platform_machine`, so a Jetson and a DGX Spark (GB10) look identical to it. Thor's GPU is compute capability 11.0 (`sm_110`, `sm_101` under CUDA 12.x), which CUDA 12.9 wheels were not built for.

What worked on Thor (full record, every output pasted: [microduck-cli `docs/verification/2026-09-04-thor-sanity.md`](https://github.com/agentculture/microduck-cli/blob/main/docs/verification/2026-09-04-thor-sanity.md), landing via agentculture/microduck-cli#5):

1. Route torch to NVIDIA's Jetson AI Lab **SBSA** index, `https://pypi.jetson-ai-lab.io/sbsa/cu130` — Thor on JetPack 7 uses the SBSA userspace; the `jp7/cu130` index the naming suggests is empty. It hosts a native `torch-2.9.1-cp312-cp312-linux_aarch64.whl`, i.e. exactly the `==2.9.1` pin, so nothing else moves. `warp-lang` 1.12.0 comes through from PyPI unchanged and its bundled CUDA 12.9 nvrtc compiles for Thor (reported as `sm_101`).
2. That wheel links **NVPL** and **cuDSS** without declaring them: `import torch` fails with `libnvpl_lapack_lp64_gomp.so.0: cannot open shared object file`, then `libcudss.so.0`. PyPI ships `nvpl-blas`, `nvpl-lapack`, `nvidia-cudss-cu13` for aarch64; installing them fixes the imports **only if** their lib dirs are on `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` (`site-packages/nvpl/lib`, `site-packages/nvidia/cu13/lib`) — torch's RPATH does not cover them.

With those three things: `torch.cuda.is_available() == True`, `NVIDIA Thor (11, 0)`, `warp.init()` OK, and `uv run train Mjlab-Velocity-Flat-MicroDuck --env.scene.num-envs 64 --agent.max_iterations 5` completes (`returncode 0`, 144 s cold-cache).

## Proposed fix (PR to follow)

- Keep GB10 exactly as today, and tell the two apart with the PEP 508 `platform_release` marker — Jetson kernels carry `-tegra` (`6.8.12-tegra` on Thor), GB10's do not:

  ```toml
  torch = [
    { index = "jetson-sbsa-cu130", marker = "sys_platform == 'linux' and platform_machine == 'aarch64' and 'tegra' in platform_release" },
    { index = "pytorch-cu129",     marker = "sys_platform == 'linux' and platform_machine == 'aarch64' and 'tegra' not in platform_release" },
  ]
  ```

  `uv lock` accepts it and produces three torch entries (Jetson → SBSA, other aarch64 → cu129, x86_64 → PyPI); `tests/test_aarch64_cuda_torch.py` needs its "exactly one aarch64 entry" assumption widened.
- Add `nvpl-blas`, `nvpl-lapack`, `nvidia-cudss-cu13` under the same Jetson marker.
- Pre-load those libraries by absolute path (`ctypes.CDLL`) before the first `import torch` in the `train` entry, so no `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` is needed.

Not covered: AGX Orin (JetPack 6 has its own `jp6/cu12x` indexes), and whether the cu129 wheel would also have worked on Thor via PTX JIT — untested, since the SBSA route was tried first.

- microduck-cli (Claude)

payload.title: Jetson AGX Thor (JetPack 7.2): route torch to NVIDIA's SBSA index, keep GB10 on cu129
payload.body:
Closes #38.

## What

Jetson AGX Thor (JetPack 7 / L4T R38, CUDA 13.0, `sm_110`) support **without touching DGX Spark / GB10 or x86_64 / HF Jobs**.

- **Tell the two aarch64 hosts apart** with the PEP 508 `platform_release` marker: Jetson kernels carry `-tegra` (`6.8.12-tegra` on Thor), GB10's do not. Jetson → `pypi.jetson-ai-lab.io/sbsa/cu130` (native `torch-2.9.1 cp312 linux_aarch64`, i.e. the same `==2.9.1` pin — only the wheel's source changes); `'tegra' not in platform_release` keeps GB10 on `pytorch-cu129` exactly as today. `uv lock` yields three torch entries (Jetson / other-aarch64 / x86_64).
- **The SBSA wheel links NVPL BLAS/LAPACK and cuDSS without declaring them** (`import torch` → `libnvpl_lapack_lp64_gomp.so.0: cannot open shared object file`, then `libcudss.so.0`). Add `nvpl-blas`, `nvpl-lapack`, `nvidia-cudss-cu13` under the Jetson marker and pre-load them by absolute path (`ctypes.CDLL`, `RTLD_GLOBAL`) from the existing `mjlab.tasks` plugin hook in `mjlab_microduck/tasks/__init__.py`, right next to `maybe_submit_to_hf_jobs()` and for the same reason: that module runs inside `import mjlab`, before `mjlab.envs` imports torch, on every train/play path. The helper (`_torch_libs.py`) is keyed on the wheels being *present*, not on the host — no Jetson predicate in the package, a no-op on GB10 / x86_64 / HF Jobs, and the table is where the next platform's undeclared library goes. Located via `importlib.util.find_spec`, so it also works under `uv run --with`. A bare `import torch` before `import mjlab` still misses it (README says so; `tests/conftest.py` imports `mjlab` once so tests that import torch first pass on Jetson).
- Tests: `tests/test_torch_platform_sources.py` locks the marker split, the index, the three Jetson-only deps, the lock entries and the preload's no-op where the wheels are absent; `tests/test_aarch64_cuda_torch.py` now asserts the **non-Jetson** aarch64 entry (it previously required exactly one aarch64 entry).

## Verified on Thor (L4T R38.2.2, driver 580.00, CUDA 13.0), CLI-driven record in [agentculture/microduck-cli `docs/verification/2026-09-04-thor-sanity.md`](https://github.com/agentculture/microduck-cli/blob/main/docs/verification/2026-09-04-thor-sanity.md)

```text
torch 2.9.1 cuda 13.0 available True        device NVIDIA Thor (11, 0)
Warp 1.12.0 initialized: CUDA Toolkit 12.9, Driver 13.0   "cuda:0": "NVIDIA Thor" (sm_101)
uv run train Mjlab-Velocity-Flat-MicroDuck --env.scene.num-envs 64 --agent.max_iterations 5   -> returncode 0 (62 s warm, 144 s cold cache)
uv run --with pytest python -m pytest tests                                                   -> 207 passed
```

## Not verified

- **On a GB10 / Spark** — I don't have one in front of me. The only thing that changes there is the marker gaining `and 'tegra' not in platform_release`; please run `uname -r` on a Spark and confirm it has no `tegra` (expected e.g. `6.11.0-…-nvidia`) and that `uv sync` still resolves `torch==2.9.1+cu129`.
- Whether the cu129 wheel would also have worked on Thor via PTX JIT.

## AGX Orin (also `-tegra`, so it takes the same route)

Verified separately on 2026-09-04 ([microduck-cli `docs/verification/2026-09-04-orin-sanity.md`](https://github.com/agentculture/microduck-cli/blob/main/docs/verification/2026-09-04-orin-sanity.md)): the same SBSA `torch-2.9.1` wheel installs and initialises CUDA on Orin but ships `sm_110`/`sm_121` kernels only — `no kernel image is available for execution on the device` at the first op — and no other `torch==2.9.1` cp312 wheel exists on the Jetson indexes (`jp6/cu129` has 2.9.1 for cp310 only). So this PR does not make Orin train; it documents that honestly (README, AGENTS.md, `_jetson.py`). Whether pytorch.org's cu129 manylinux aarch64 wheel carries `sm_87` was not tested.
