payload.title: fix: route torch to a CUDA index on aarch64 (DGX Spark / GB10)
payload.body:
## Problem

Every `train` command dies on a DGX Spark (GB10, aarch64) before iteration 0:

```
File "mjlab/utils/gpu.py", line 70, in select_gpus
  selected_gpus = [available_gpus[i] for i in gpu_ids]
IndexError: list index out of range
```

## Root cause

Nothing was wrong with the GPU — warp saw `cuda:0` (sm_121, 122 GiB) the whole
time. Only torch was blind.

On linux-aarch64, PyPI's torch wheel is **CPU-only**: `torch.__version__` is
`2.9.1+cpu` and `torch.version.cuda` is `None`. So `torch.cuda.device_count()`
returns 0, `select_gpus()` builds an empty `available_gpus`, and indexing it
raises. The traceback points at GPU *selection*, which sends you looking at
drivers and `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`; the actual fault is which wheel got
installed.

## Fix

Route torch to PyTorch's cu129 index, scoped by marker to aarch64 only.

**cu129 rather than cu130** because it matches the CUDA toolkit warp 1.12.0
bundles (warp reports "CUDA Toolkit 12.9"), keeping mjlab's zero-copy
warp↔torch interop on one runtime major version.

Two details this depends on. Both are silent when broken — `uv sync` succeeds
and you only find out at launch:

1. **torch must be a DIRECT dependency.** uv applies `[tool.uv.sources]` to
   direct deps only, so while torch arrived purely via mjlab/rsl_rl the index
   was ignored with no warning. The `torch==` line looks redundant; it isn't.
2. **The pin must be `==`, not `>=`.** The CUDA index carries newer builds than
   the PyPI pin, so `torch>=2.7.0` pulled 2.9.1 → 2.13.0 (and torchvision →
   0.28.0). `==2.9.1` changes only the wheel's source, not its version.

## HF Jobs are unaffected

Verified, not assumed. Evaluating every package's `resolution-markers` against
an x86_64-linux env and diffing `develop` vs this branch:

```
packages resolving on x86_64-linux:  develop=142  branch=142
  added: (none)   removed: (none)   changed: (none)
torch on x86 -> [('2.9.1', 'https://pypi.org/simple')]
x86 packages sourced from the CUDA index: (none)
```

Identical package for package. All three HF flavors (`l4x1`, `a10g-large`,
`a100-large`) are x86_64, `uv lock --check` passes so the container resolves
straight from the lock without re-resolving, and the persistent uv cache stays
warm.

The large `uv.lock` diff is mostly uv annotating explicit `version`/`source` on
transitive packages now that two resolution branches exist. The real change is
the torch entry splitting in two:

| resolution-markers | source | version |
|---|---|---|
| `platform_machine != 'aarch64' or sys_platform != 'linux'` | pypi.org | `2.9.1` |
| `platform_machine == 'aarch64' and sys_platform == 'linux'` | download.pytorch.org/whl/cu129 | `2.9.1+cu129` |

## Regression guards

`tests/test_aarch64_cuda_torch.py` locks both silent failure modes plus the
x86_64 side. Five tests parse `pyproject.toml`/`uv.lock` and run anywhere (CPU,
no GPU); the sixth self-skips unless on ARM with a working `nvidia-smi`, where
it asserts `torch.cuda.device_count() > 0` — a direct reproduction of the crash.

The guards were verified to **fail against the pre-fix `pyproject.toml`/`uv.lock`**,
not merely to pass here.

## Test plan

Run on the DGX Spark from a **deleted `.venv`**, to exercise the clean-clone
path that originally failed:

- [x] fresh `uv sync` → 142 packages
- [x] torch `2.9.1+cu129`, cuda 12.9, 1 device, 4096² GPU matmul
- [x] `pytest tests/` → **155 passed**
- [x] smoke test (64 envs / 5 iters) → `device=cuda:0`, `nan_state: 0.0000`
- [x] **the original failing command** (4096 envs, 20 iters) → ~2.67 s/iter,
      reward 2.06 → 2.36, no NaN
- [x] ONNX export from checkpoint → input `obs [1, 61]`, output `actions [1, 14]`,
      finite (61D actor obs invariant holds)

## Notes for reviewers

torch prints a startup warning on GB10, and it is expected:

```
Found GPU0 NVIDIA GB10 which is of cuda capability 12.1.
Minimum and Maximum cuda capability supported by this version of PyTorch is (8.0) - (12.0)
```

torch 2.9.1's arch list tops out at `sm_120`; GB10 is `sm_121`, and sm_120
cubins are family-compatible — confirmed by real matmuls and full 4096-env
training steps. When bumping torch, prefer a release with native sm_121. If a
`no kernel image is available` error ever appears, switching the index URL to
`cu130` provides `compute_120` PTX JIT fallback (that build was tested working
on this GPU too).

No CI workflow is included (deliberate — repo has none today), so the guards
run only when someone runs pytest. No `src/` changes: RL training behavior is
byte-identical.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

For a contact-based pinch-and-lift test, the missing piece is how the two beak contact surfaces move relative to one another as the mouth command changes. The public ground-contact model merges the jaw meshes into the head body, while the runtime controls the mouth independently.

The smallest useful data would be the moving-part membership, joint pivot/axis and zero/sign, actuator-to-jaw linkage or transmission, and travel limits. Per-link masses/inertias and mouth actuator details would also help preserve the stock dynamics.

We hit this too on a single RTX 4070 (4096 envs), and I think I can add two data points that aren't in your matrix. Our run converges to error_vel_xy ~= 0.42, so the same place as yours at 0.43.

**1. The air_time gate only looks at the command, not at whether the robot is actually moving.**

```python
# mjlab/tasks/velocity/mdp/rewards.py:L209
def feet_air_time(env, sensor_name, threshold_min=0.05, threshold_max=0.5,
                  command_name=None, command_threshold=0.5):
    ...
    if command_name is not None:
        total_command = torch.norm(command[:, :2], dim=1) + torch.abs(command[:, 2])
        scale = (total_command > command_threshold).float()
        reward *= scale
    return reward
```

`microduck_velocity_env_cfg.py` sets `command_threshold = 0.01`, so any non-zero command passes. A policy that is commanded forward but only steps in place keeps collecting this reward at weight 3.0, which is the largest positive weight in the set.

This may be why your matrix didn't isolate it: you report `air_time ≈ 0.002`, feet never leaving the ground. Ours is `0.9997`, feet leaving constantly but the body not translating. It is a different position in the same basin, and the "step in place and get paid" route is available.

Gating on achieved motion instead (only pay when horizontal speed reaches ~30% of the commanded horizontal speed) took error_vel_xy from 0.43 to 0.35.

**2. The body-frame velocity is dominated by lateral drift, and the tracking reward treats both axes equally.**

Stepping one env with a constant command of `(+0.30, 0.00)` and reading `root_link_lin_vel_b` each step:

| step | forward | lateral |
|---|---|---|
| 3 | +0.044 | -0.056 |
| 5 | +0.072 | -0.149 |
| 7 | +0.112 | **-0.230** |

Lateral drift reaches twice the forward speed. `track_linear_velocity` computes `(cmd_x - v_x)^2 + (cmd_y - v_y)^2`, so it has no reason to prefer fixing the lateral component. Weighting lateral error 3x and raising the tracking weight from 2.0 to 4.0 dropped lateral drift to -0.044 while forward speed stayed the same, and error_vel_xy went to 0.21.

**3. A caution about error_vel_xy as the success signal.**

`velocity_command.py:L64` accumulates

```python
torch.norm(vel_command_b[:, :2] - root_link_lin_vel_b[:, :2], dim=-1) / max_command_step
```

over the whole episode and across all five command modes (standing, heading, world, forward, plain). Measuring the same checkpoint frame by frame over 400 steps gives a steady-state error of **0.07**, while the logged metric reads **0.206**. The metric averages in the ramp-up (error ~0.30 at reset) and the other command modes.

That is roughly a 3x overestimate. It also means the logged number cannot tell you which mode is failing, which is consistent with your matrix being inconclusive on experiments 1 and 3: a run can briefly discover a gait (your 0.15 at iter 1565, our 0.10) and still show a flat 0.4 because the other modes hold the average up.

**Caveats.** Single run per configuration, no seeds, so part of the 0.43 to 0.21 drop could be run-to-run variance. The 30% gate threshold is a guess with no sensitivity analysis. And the steady-state 0.07 is one checkpoint and one reset, though 16 samples across 8 s agree.

**Clip (stand → flop onto the back → hold)**  
https://github.com/SAMBAS123/microduck_rl/releases/download/playdead-clip-iter1999/playdead_iter1999.mp4

| | |
|---|---|
| standing spawn | after the flop |
| ![stand](https://github.com/SAMBAS123/microduck_rl/releases/download/playdead-clip-iter1999/playdead_stand.jpg) | ![hold](https://github.com/SAMBAS123/microduck_rl/releases/download/playdead-clip-iter1999/playdead_hold.jpg) |

Trunk parks at **46 mm** and stays there (face-up rest is ~44 mm; sit is 60 mm).

### Tests

```text
uv run --with pytest pytest tests/          # 171 passed (CPU), including tests/test_playdead_cfg.py (16)
uv run train Mjlab-PlayDead-Flat-MicroDuck \
  --env.scene.num-envs 64 --agent.max_iterations 5
# smoke: actor obs (61,), every reward term computed, Episode_Termination/nan_state = 0
# ONNX export 61 → 14
```

### 2000-iter run (Spark / GB10)

```text
uv run train Mjlab-PlayDead-Flat-MicroDuck --env.scene.num-envs 4096 --agent.max_iterations 2000
```

- exit 0, `nan_state = 0` the whole way
- mean reward ~40.7
- `playdead_hold` ~1.85 (term weight 2.0)
- `playdead_composite` ~2.75
- plateaued by ~iter 400; the rest was polish

`infer_policy.py --playdead … --headless --auto-playdead --video` is how the mp4 was cut. Replay:

```bash
uv run python scripts/infer_policy.py \
  --playdead playdead.onnx --new-cmd-obs \
  --headless --auto-playdead --video playdead.mp4 --video-seconds 6
```
Good idea :+1:

## Throughput benchmark on DGX Spark (GB10)

Numbers for this branch on the target hardware. Before the fix there is nothing
to compare against — `train` crashed in `select_gpus()` before iteration 0, so
throughput was effectively zero on this machine.

**Setup**: `Mjlab-Velocity-Flat-MicroDuck`, torch `2.9.1+cu129`, warp 1.12.0
(CUDA 12.9), driver 580.173.02, NVIDIA GB10 (sm_121, aarch64), 25 iterations per
config with the first 5 discarded as warmup (warp kernel load + cache).
`env-steps/s = num_envs × 24 / iter_time` (`NUM_STEPS_PER_ENV = 24`).

| envs | iter time | env-steps/s | 4000 iters (est.) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 512 | 0.860 s | 14,288 | 0.96 h |
| 1024 | 1.018 s | 24,153 | 1.13 h |
| 2048 | 1.464 s | 33,585 | 1.63 h |
| **4096** | **2.672 s** | **36,784** | **2.97 h** |
| 8192 | 6.535 s | 30,085 | 7.26 h |
| 16384 | 19.782 s | 19,877 | 21.98 h |

Timings are highly reproducible — steady-state standard deviation is 0.008 s at
4096, 0.022 s at 8192, 0.015 s at 16384. Only iteration 1 shows warmup cost.
Every config ran on `device=cuda:0` with `nan_state: 0.0000` and no errors.

### Findings

**4096 envs is the throughput sweet spot** at ~36.8k env-steps/s, which is
already the default in the README. Past that it degrades rather than plateaus:
8192 gives 18% *fewer* steps/s than 4096, and 16384 gives 46% fewer. 16384 costs
3.0× the per-iteration time of 8192 for 2× the envs, which looks like GB10's
unified memory becoming the bottleneck. There is no reason to raise `--num-envs`
above 4096 on this box.

Scaling is only strong up to ~2048 (512 → 2048 gains 2.35× throughput for 4×
the envs); 2048 → 4096 gains just 9%.

### Caveat on wall-clock estimates

The last column is `iter_time × 4000` and assumes constant per-iteration cost —
it is arithmetic, not a measured full run. CLAUDE.md budgets gaits at 4000–6000
iterations, so a full walking run at 4096 envs lands around **3–4.5 h** here.
That sits above the README's "~1–2 h for a usable gait at 4096 envs", which was
presumably measured on a faster x86 GPU (or counts "usable" well before 4000
iterations). Worth a follow-up to reconcile, but out of scope for this PR — I
have not trained a gait to completion on this hardware to check.

Sourced from hono's releases.

v4.13.13

Mount Middleware

app.mount() is now available as the Mount Middleware, hono/mount. It is just a handler, so you register it with app.all():

import { Router as IttyRouter } from 'itty-router'
import { Hono } from 'hono'
import { mount } from 'hono/mount'

const ittyRouter = IttyRouter()

ittyRouter.get('/hello', () => new Response('Hello from itty-router'))


const app = new Hono()

app.all('/itty-router/*', mount(ittyRouter.handle))

app.mount() still works in v4 but is deprecated and will be removed in v5. Migrating is a one-line change:

- app.mount('/itty-router', ittyRouter.handle)

Release notes

vinext@1.0.0-beta.10

This release includes a new caching library for apps targeting Cloudflare Workers, called Workers Response Store. It is designed to fill the gaps that our other Cloudflare cache adapters struggled with; efficient cache warming, durable backing stores, stable ISR and revalidation, and better internal control of the cache.

To find out more, check out our caching docs. Going forward, the Workers Response Store will be our recommended choice for caching due to the flexibility it provides, and over the coming weeks it shall be stabilised following community feedback.

Build

  • select adapter-owned worker stages (#3150)

Updates `@vitejs/plugin-react` from 6.0.2 to 6.1.1
Release notes

Sourced from @​vitejs/plugin-react's releases.

plugin-react@6.1.1

Add compiler.logDiagnostics option

Recoverable React Compiler diagnostics are no longer logged by default. Set compiler.logDiagnostics to true to log them through Vite. Fatal diagnostics are always logged and fail the transform.

Respect environment sourcemap option for React Compiler transform when builder.sharedPlugins is enabled (#1439)

The React Compiler transform was using the top-level sourcemap option instead of the environment sourcemap option. This caused a problem when the experimental builder.sharedPlugins was enabled.

plugin-react@6.1.0

Add experimental native React Compiler support (#1419)

Add experimental native React Compiler support.

You can use it by installing oxc-transform-react and enabling it via the compiler option:

npm install -D oxc-transform-react

import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react'

export default defineConfig({

plugins: [

react({ compiler: true })

]

})

plugin-react@6.0.5

Fixed the react compiler preset filter to be linear (#1353)

The improved filter in v6.0.3 was non-linear and caused a performance regression (#1349). The filter was changed to be linear to avoid that.

plugin-react@6.0.4

Fixed $RefreshSig$ is not defined error when running vite dev with NODE_ENV=production

When running vite dev with NODE_ENV=production, the app errored with $RefreshSig$ is not defined. This error is now fixed.

plugins: [

react({ compiler: true })

payload.title: Harden v0.2 preview accuracy, safety, and mobile UX
payload.body:
The v0.2 preview had several credibility and runtime gaps: some reinforcement-learning explanations were imprecise, imported profiles were trusted without schema validation, Academy mode still allowed upstream multiplayer networking, and switching from rollers back to legs could crash the pinned simulator build.

This patch tightens the curriculum and product claims, validates local profiles, makes the embedded simulator local-only by default, hardens the launcher and shutdown service, repairs the pinned simulator locomotion handoff during local builds, and fixes the real 390 px mobile layout. It also documents the exact 25-entry `control.duck` surface without presenting it as the complete upstream Microduck API.

Validation:
- `npm run setup:runtime` (upstream simulator tests and production build)
- `npm run verify` (release/docs checks, 16 tests, lint, typecheck, production build)
- real-browser completion of all 9 lessons and 6 policy-inspection experiments
- real-browser Level 2 execution across continuous control, feedback blocks, built-in skills, base switching, community-policy loading, and recovery
- real MuJoCo Level 3 reward rollout
- Chinese/English switching, profile export/import, and reload persistence
- desktop and 390 px responsive Chrome visual inspection with no horizontal overflow

Release boundary remains explicit: this is a public preview through Level 3. PPO weight updates, ONNX export, and physical-device deployment are still roadmap work.

payload.name: Microduck Academy v0.2.1 Preview
payload.body:
This patch release is the result of a full pre-launch audit of the bilingual course, simulator bridge, local data boundary, mobile layout, and repository presentation.

## What changed

- Corrected RL explanations for goal-conditioned control, discounted return, PPO clipping, reward exploits, and hardware safety limits.
- Corrected the Level 2 projected-gravity example and made rejected simulator actions report an error.
- Documented the exact 25-entry Academy `control.duck` surface and its verified Hub / HTTPS ONNX inputs.
- Added schema validation for imported browser-local learning profiles.
- Disabled upstream multiplayer signaling and pose broadcast in Academy embedded mode.
- Hardened local service discovery, port conflicts, shutdown origin checks, and the macOS launcher.
- Patched the pinned simulator build so rollers → legs switching preserves the leg joint addresses.
- Repaired the true 390 px mobile viewport and narrow-screen layout.

## 已修复

- 修正目标条件控制、折扣回报、PPO 裁剪、reward exploit 和真机安全限制等课程表述。
- 修正 Level 2 投影重力示例；模拟器拒绝动作时会明确报错。
- 明确 Academy 当前 25 项 `control.duck` API，以及已核对的 Hub / HTTPS ONNX 输入。
- 导入浏览器本地学习档案前校验版本与字段。
- Academy 嵌入模式关闭上游多人 signaling 和姿态广播。
- 加固本地服务识别、端口冲突、关闭来源检查和 macOS 启动器。
- 修复固定模拟器版本从滚轮切回双腿时的关节地址问题。
- 修复真实 390 px 移动端 viewport 和窄屏布局。

## Verification / 验证

`npm run verify` passes all release and documentation checks, 16 tests, lint, TypeScript, and the production build. The full 9-lesson course, 6 policy-inspection experiments, Level 2 command surface, Level 3 real MuJoCo rollout, bilingual profile persistence, and desktop/mobile browser layouts were exercised locally.

## Install / 安装

Requirements: Node.js 22+, Git, and Git LFS.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/kingsleyli920/microduck-academy.git
cd microduck-academy
npm ci
npm run setup:runtime
npm run verify
npm run academy
```

Open `http://localhost:3210`.

## Current boundary / 当前边界

This remains a preview through Level 3. It evaluates and composes existing ONNX policies. PPO weight updates, ONNX export, and physical Microduck deployment remain planned Levels 4–6 and have not been hardware-verified.

当前仍是完成到 Level 3 的 Preview，可观察、编排和评估现有 ONNX policy。PPO 权重更新、ONNX 导出和 Microduck 真机部署仍属于 Level 4–6 路线图，尚未完成真机验证。

The release contains Academy-owned source only. Generated simulator assets and official policies are built locally from pinned upstream inputs.

payload.name: Microduck Academy v0.2 Preview
payload.body:
Microduck Academy v0.2 is a bilingual, local-first reinforcement learning classroom built around the official Microduck MuJoCo + ONNX simulator.

## What is included

- Chinese and English UI, lessons, 3D labs, API reference, and core repository documentation
- Nine browser-local Python lessons covering reward, observation, action, rollout, return, PPO, reward exploits, and deployment safety
- A live 61D observation → ONNX policy → 14D action monitor
- A bounded `control.duck` language with 25 documented API entries and in-editor search
- A Task & Reward Lab for comparing reward and termination configurations with real MuJoCo rollouts
- Local learning profiles with JSON import and export; no account required
- CI, bilingual consistency tests, contribution templates, architecture documentation, and reproducible runtime setup

## 本版本内容

- 中英文课堂界面、课程、3D 实验室、API Reference 和核心仓库文档
- 9 节浏览器 Python 课程，覆盖 reward、observation、action、rollout、return、PPO、reward exploit 和部署安全
- 实时 61D observation → ONNX policy → 14D action 监视器
- 包含 25 项完整文档和编辑器内搜索的 `control.duck` 控制语言
- 使用真实 MuJoCo rollout 比较 reward 与 termination 配置的 Task & Reward Lab
- 无需登录的本地学习档案，以及 JSON 导入和导出
- CI、双语一致性测试、贡献模板、架构文档和可复现运行时安装

## Install / 安装

Requirements: Node.js 22+, Git, and Git LFS.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/kingsleyli920/microduck-academy.git
cd microduck-academy
npm ci
npm run setup:runtime
npm run verify
npm run academy
```

Open `http://localhost:3210`.

## Current boundary / 当前边界

This remains a preview. Level 3 evaluates an existing official policy; it does not update ONNX weights. PPO training, ONNX export, and physical Microduck deployment are planned Levels 4–6. Hardware behavior is not yet verified.

当前仍为 Preview。Level 3 评估已有官方 policy，不更新 ONNX 权重。PPO 训练、ONNX 导出和 Microduck 真机部署属于规划中的 Level 4–6，尚未完成真机验证。

The repository distributes Academy-owned source only. Generated simulator assets and official policies are fetched locally from pinned upstream inputs and are not included in this release.

# Duck on Desk v1.2.0

第一课「行走」改为原样嵌入官方 mjlab 训练环境，应用内直接复现官方训练流程。

- 训练环境不再是自研的 CPU MuJoCo + 自定义 PPO，而是官方仓库 `pollen-robotics/microduck_rl`（commit `53b8971`，mjlab 1.3.0 / rsl_rl 5.0.1）的 `Mjlab-Velocity-Flat-MicroDuck` 任务：16 项奖励、域随机化、特权 critic、在线观测标准化、自适应 KL 的 PPO 与课程表全部沿用官方，策略从随机权重开始。
- 一套应用两种机器：Apple Silicon 上物理在 CPU（MuJoCo Warp 没有 Metal 后端）、网络在 MPS；NVIDIA 上走官方 CUDA。界面操作不变，仍由「用哪个设备训练」决定。
- 环境安装改为克隆钉死 commit 的官方仓库并按其 `uv.lock` 执行 `uv sync --frozen`，需要本机有 Git（macOS 装 Xcode 命令行工具，Windows 装 Git for Windows）。Windows CUDA 会额外把 torch 2.9.1 换成 cu128 wheel（PyPI 的 Windows torch 是纯 CPU）。
- 第 2 步的奖励编辑框对行走课改为 `reward_weights` 权重字典，列出官方 16 项默认值；三个滑块对应 `track_linear_velocity`、`upright`、`action_rate_l2`。`action_rate_l2` 与 `head_pose_bias` 官方由课程表调整，一旦写出权重即固定，manifest 记录 `curricula_disabled`。
- 「新训练的起点」与「PPO 更新方式」对行走课隐藏并固定为官方配方；倒立课程不受影响，继续在同一个环境里跑 CPU MuJoCo 路径。
- 行走默认 256 环境 × 24 步、学习率 0.001、seed 42、200 轮；CUDA 下「使用本机推荐参数」填回官方 4096 × 24。旧 `workbench.json` 的行走设置一律忽略。
- 训练指标新增每回合平均时长、完成回合数、学习率、动作标准差、各损失项与官方逐项奖励分解；检查点为 rsl_rl 格式并附带环境步数与课程表进度，续训后轮数与步数连续。
- 官方导出的 ONNX（标准化已烘焙进图）由桌宠运行时零改动加载；训练前后的对比测试仍在应用自带的 CPU MuJoCo 环境里进行。
- MCP：`physics_backend` 新增 `"mjlab"`，行走草稿默认该值；`lab_experiment_validate` 接受只声明 `reward_weights` 的 reward.py。

本机（Apple Silicon）实测：Warp CPU 物理约 640 env-steps/s，256 环境每轮约 11 s，200 轮约 37 分钟，只适合验证流程与配置；官方规模（4096 × 24 × 50000 轮）需在 NVIDIA 机器复现。CUDA 分支按官方脚本接入 `cuda:0`，**尚未在实机验证**。Windows 11 开启「智能应用控制」的机器会拦截 `warp.dll`（WinError 4551），需关闭该功能（不可逆）或改用 WSL2；两者都未接入应用。

实测数据与未验证项见 `docs/diagnostics/mjlab-embedded-training-2026-09-11.md`。

payload.name: Duck on Desk v1.1.4
payload.body:
# Duck on Desk v1.1.4

第二课从「静态保持 2 秒倒立」改为「翻倒后用脚蹬回来」的循环练习。

- 奖励整体重写。旧奖励的验收要求双脚离地，脚一沾地保持计时立即归零——而脚正是用来蹬回去的，这个动作在原设计里无法得分。新奖励取消保持计时器与角速度惩罚，脚触地不再扣分。
- 倒置程度的计分在 −0.8 处饱和。实测「折叠在自己头上」这种失败姿态比可持续的目标姿态更倒（−0.92 对 −0.80），继续为更大倒置加分会把失败排在目标之前。躯干高度是两者唯一的判别量（0.04 对 0.078），已作为计分因子。
- 新增恢复计分：每次真实跌倒后回到头部贴地给一次奖励，环境内以滞回判定，避免临界抖动被计入。只靠摆一个姿势不动的策略拿不到这一项。
- 环境新增参考状态初始化：从翻倒过程的随机时刻起步。此前只有「顶端平衡」和「完全趴地」两种状态会被采样，中间的小幅修正从未练到，约 96% 的样本来自躺地状态。
- 训练新增探索噪声保持步数。逐步独立噪声在多步蹬地动作上相互抵消，连贯的蹬地动作采不到。第二课默认保持 4 步。
- 第二课默认定时重置由 1500 步（30 秒）改为 120 步（2.4 秒），并默认开启随机起步。
- 验收指标改为循环口径：头部贴地时间占比、躺地占比、恢复次数、最长一次时长。旧的 2 秒静态保持无法登记这一行为。

第一课行走、第三课倒立进入与街舞课的奖励和验收标准均未改动。续训历史记录保留其原有奖励、重置规则与轮次长度。

本机 MPS 训练已复现目标行为，但 **3 个种子中只有 1 个成功**（约 140 万采样步、25 分钟）。成功的策略保持头部贴地、躯干高度 0.074、躯干不触地；把控制器切断 0.9 秒让它在重力下摔到 `upright +0.03` 后恢复控制，能爬回头部贴地并在结尾持续稳住。另外 2 个种子停在「折叠在自己头上」——躯干高度只有 0.050~0.054，摔倒后再也起不来。所以这是一个**能训出来但不稳定**的配方。

验收因此改为真实的击倒测试：评测中途切断控制器 0.9 秒，必须先真的摔下去（`upright > -0.2`），再回到头部贴地并稳住结尾 0.5 秒才算通过。只按「头朝下的时间占比」判定会把折叠姿态判为成功。

奖励另经 CEM-MPC 规划器从「近倒立」与「已经趴下」两个起点独立验证，最优解确实是目标行为（头部贴地时间 83.5% / 92.3%）。验收阈值仍是照规划器可达值设定的暂定值。CUDA 仍待 NVIDIA 实机验证。

分析、实测数据与方法教训见 `docs/diagnostics/headstand-cycle-reward-2026-09-10.md`。

payload.name: Duck on Desk v1.1.3
payload.body:
# Duck on Desk v1.1.3

机器人实验室的训练参数由用户决定，默认值不再作为强制范围。

- 移除新建训练、续训追加及累计训练轮数的人为上限，不再两小时自动停止。按填写的轮数训练，也可手动停止保存后继续。
- 移除同时练习的机器人数量、每轮采样步数、定时重置间隔的人为上限；界面、MCP 和训练程序使用相同规则。
- 放开学习率、目标速度和随机种子的原有范围限制。保留有效数字、正整数等必要校验；默认参数不变。
- 奖励权重改为数字输入，支持自定义数值；实验室预览不再把前进与转弯指令截断到旧范围。
- 支持单个样本的短轮次训练，修复小学习率或零学习率导致参数未变化时无法导出的问题。参数变化量仍如实记录，非有限数值继续报错。
- 保留 PPO 裁剪公式、官方网络结构和机器人模型定义的关节物理范围。

已验证真实 CPU 短训、检查点与 ONNX 导出，包括 64 个环境、300 步采样及单样本配置；这些验证不代表动作已学会，也不保证任意规模都能在当前硬件上运行。CUDA 训练仍待 NVIDIA 实机验证。

payload.name: Duck on Desk v1.1.2
payload.body:
# Duck on Desk v1.1.2

修复新机器首次训练提示 `Microduck model / base policy unavailable; install model assets first` 的问题。

- 训练开始前自动补齐固定版本的 Microduck 基础策略，保存到用户 Hugging Face 缓存。训练服务不再记住不存在的旧包内路径。
- “Python 环境”留空即可自动安装独立的 Python 3.12、PyTorch、MuJoCo 与 ONNX 依赖；也可点击“检查 / 安装训练环境”提前准备。已有自定义环境只检查，不修改。
- Windows x64 默认 CUDA，Apple Silicon 默认 MPS。CUDA 安装使用 PyTorch 2.9.1 / CUDA 12.8 wheel；启动前检查实际 GPU 计算。不可用时显示原因，不自动退回 CPU。
- 首次下载和环境检查显示进度，失败后可重试；训练的准备阶段也可以停止。MCP 新增环境安装与状态查询接口。
- 修复 Windows 默认编码无法读取中文训练配置和奖励脚本的问题，统一使用 UTF-8。
- 保留 1.1.1 的默认 30 秒重置、可配置重置时间与历史续训设置。

首次安装需要网络及可用磁盘空间，CUDA 依赖下载较大。CUDA 需要受支持的 NVIDIA 显卡和驱动；本版自动安装不代替显卡驱动安装。自动环境支持 Windows x64、Apple Silicon；Intel Mac / Windows ARM 用户可填写自行配置的 Python。CUDA 实际训练仍待 NVIDIA 机器验证，Windows CPU 验证不能代替它。

payload.name: Duck on Desk v1.1.1
payload.body:
# Duck on Desk 1.1.1

机器人实验室加入可配置的训练重置时间，并正式发布此前在本地验证的训练、续训和关节控制功能。

- 第二课「倒立保持」默认每 **30 秒模拟时间**回到近倒立初态。在「开始练习」步骤可设置 0～1000 秒，0 表示关闭定时重置。身体倾斜、脚触地时仍可以尝试蹬地恢复。
- 训练记录显示实际使用的重置规则。继续训练恢复权重、优化器、仿真和随机状态，沿用原记录的参数；修改界面时间只影响新训练。
- 四步强化学习教程、完整自定义奖励、奖励分项、策略／价值 loss 曲线，以及默认关闭的真实训练 3D 预览。
- 14 路关节输出中文映射、半透明模型和即时手动摆姿；镜头跟随机器人移动。实验室使用独立普通窗口，支持 Dock／任务栏切换。
- 两课使用官方同构策略网络；行走默认加载官方权重，倒立默认随机初始化。PPO 支持分批更新、自适应学习率和 MPS；CUDA 接口保留，尚待 NVIDIA 实机验证。
- Duck 右键动作菜单支持预置啄地及行走时随机动作。倒立基础练习仍为实验课程，未训练成功，不会自动替换桌宠行走或加入动作库。
- 安装包不复制模型权重；首次使用所需策略时下载固定版本到用户级 Hugging Face 缓存，之后复用。首次使用需要网络。

从「设置 → 关于 → 打开开发者模式」进入实验室。训练需要已有的 PyTorch、MuJoCo、ONNX 和 ONNX Runtime Python 环境。现有模型、训练记录及自定义奖励保留。

提供 macOS Apple Silicon／Intel 和 Windows arm64／x64 安装包。macOS 使用 ad-hoc 签名，未公证；Windows 窗口切换与 CUDA 的实机验证仍待完成。仿真训练和软件验证不代表实体机器人安全验收。

payload.name: Duck on Desk v1.0.0
payload.body:
# Duck on Desk 1.0.0

这次更新把机器人实验室带进正式安装版，并重新整理了「关于」页面的开发者入口和项目署名。

## 开发者模式与机器人实验室

- 在「设置 → 关于」开启「打开开发者模式」，进入独立的 3D 机器人实验室。开关默认关闭，保存后跨重启保留；窗口关掉后可从同一页面再次进入。
- 完整机器人、地面和轨道相机，支持运行、暂停、单步、重置以及 14 个关节的检查和手动控制。
- 可编辑奖励脚本与策略网络，设置 PPO 训练参数，查看实际采样步数和奖励曲线，停止任务并保留历史。
- 训练后可预览候选策略，完成原生与浏览器物理评测，再应用到普通脚桌宠；支持导出 ONNX 和恢复上一策略。
- Agent 管理页可以为 Claude Code、Codex CLI、OpenCode 安装 Robot Lab MCP。Coding Agent 可查询接口文档、版本化写入奖励／策略脚本、启动和管理真实训练任务。

训练需要自行选择装有 torch、mujoco、onnx、onnxruntime 的 Python 环境。物理使用 CPU MuJoCo，训练和 Python 评测推理可分别选择 MPS、CUDA、CPU；桌宠及实验室预览仍用 Web WASM。MPS 已实测，CUDA 待 NVIDIA 实机验证。第一版支持平地普通脚的 PPO 动作修正，尚未提供自动续训或任意 RL 算法插件。

关闭开发者模式会销毁实验室窗口；已启动的训练继续，由所属 App 或 MCP 进程管理。退出所属进程会停止其任务。默认不开启实验室，也不会自动训练或提交付费云作业。

## 关于页面

- 本项目作者、维护者和贡献者更新为 **Happenmass**。
- 上游 Clawd on Desk 作者、维护者及贡献者移入「上游项目与致谢」，保留 Pollen Robotics 来源及现有授权说明。
- 发布下载按平台分别获取并核对大小、SHA-512 和更新元数据，防止截断安装包进入更新通道。

## 验证与更新

本机已通过 MPS 20 轮、2,560 个真实物理步的训练、ONNX 导出、浏览器评测，以及隔离 Electron 虚拟桌宠中的实际加载、导出和回退。短训证明链路有效，不代表步态已经明显改善。Windows 和 CUDA 尚未进行本机硬件验收。

v0.2.3 用户可以在「设置 → 关于」检查更新。v0.2.2 及更早版本的更新地址有误，需要手动下载本次安装包；替换应用不会主动清空已有设置。macOS 安装包沿用 ad-hoc 签名，未作 Developer ID 公证。

本更新不包含实体机器人硬件安全验收。程序代码为 AGPL-3.0-only；机器人资产的单独授权和非商业使用边界见仓库 NOTICE.md。

payload.name: Duck on Desk v0.2.3
payload.body:
# v0.2.3

Checking for updates works. It never had, in any release of this fork.

- The update check asked GitHub for releases of `rullerzhou-afk/duck-on-desk`.
  That repository does not exist — the owner was inherited from the upstream
  project this fork is derived from and left hardcoded, while the builds were
  published here. Every check got a 404, which the app reported as "Duck 更新时
  遇到未知错误 / No releases found". Checks now go to `Happenmass/duck-on-desk`,
  where the releases actually are
- Settings -> About linked the same nonexistent repository. It now points at
  this fork's source, which is what a user needs for the build they are running.
  The upstream author credit, copyright and AGPL-3.0 license are unchanged
- A test now ties the update URL to the `build.publish` target in
  `package.json`, so the two cannot drift apart again

**Updating from 0.2.2 or earlier has to be done once by hand.** The fix lives in
the new build, so an installed 0.2.2 still asks the dead repository and still
reports the same error — it cannot see this release. Download the installer
below once; automatic checks work from 0.2.3 onward.

No behaviour, rendering or physics changes in this release.

macOS (arm64/x64 dmg+zip) and Windows (x64/arm64 NSIS).

Not real-machine validated on Windows or Linux for this release; the update
check was verified against the live GitHub API and the smoke pass was done on
macOS arm64.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/Happenmass/duck-on-desk/compare/v0.2.2...v0.2.3

payload.name: Duck on Desk v0.2.2
payload.body:
# v0.2.2

The 3D pet costs about half the CPU it used to while it is just standing there.

- The renderer ran at whatever the display offered — 120 fps on a ProMotion
  panel — and drew all 70 rig meshes a second time every frame for a real
  shadow map. Both robot runtimes now render at 30 fps, and the shadow map is
  replaced by a painted blob under the feet at the same size and weight
- Measured on an M-series Mac with a 120 Hz display, the duck idling: total app
  CPU 53.8% of a core -> 26.5% (2 samples before, 10 after; before was tight at
  53.3-54.2%, after spreads 23.2-30.5% because the remaining cost now tracks
  what the duck is doing rather than the frame rate). The GPU process alone
  falls 25.5% -> 8.4%. The win is smaller on a 60 Hz display, where the frame
  cap has half as much to remove. Memory is unchanged
- The physics and the control policy were never the expensive part: MuJoCo plus
  the ONNX policy measure ~1.1% of a core together, so nothing about how the
  duck balances, walks, falls or gets picked up has changed
- The camera's ease-down after the duck is dropped is now driven by elapsed
  time instead of by frame count. It had been a flat factor per rendered frame,
  which silently tied the settle to the display's refresh rate and would have
  stretched it four-fold under the new frame cap

macOS (arm64/x64 dmg+zip) and Windows (x64/arm64 NSIS).

Not real-machine validated on Windows or Linux for this release; the
measurements and the smoke pass were done on macOS arm64.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/Happenmass/duck-on-desk/compare/v0.2.1...v0.2.2

payload.name: Duck on Desk v0.2.1
payload.body:
# v0.2.1

A fix for the duck freezing after a restart, and new step sounds.

- The 3D duck no longer stands still after the app restarts or the renderer reloads while a session is already working: main now re-sends the current state once the renderer's MuJoCo/ONNX runtime is listening, instead of the on-load message being dropped and the duck waiting on a 9.75 s retry that could be dropped too
- Steps and landings are now single moves of a real hobby servo ("Small servo (arduino)" by gpag1, CC0 on freesound) instead of the Kenney footstep and thump samples; NOTICE and the READMEs credit the new source, and the "Duck footsteps" setting describes the servo whine
- A test pins that every servo take the audio adapter can pick is shipped, since a missing take only logs a warning

macOS (arm64/x64 dmg+zip) and Windows (x64/arm64 NSIS).

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/Happenmass/duck-on-desk/compare/v0.2.0...v0.2.1

payload.name: Duck on Desk v0.2.0
payload.body:
# v0.2.0

Adds Reachy Mini as a second robot: a physical Reachy Mini on the LAN, a 3D virtual one on the desktop, or both mirrored.

- Physical Reachy Mini support: mDNS or manual host discovery, auto-connect, and a "Robot" section in Settings and the tray menu
- Robot wake/sleep is driven by the semantic state machine and calls the official daemon moves (`wake_up`, `goto_sleep`), with motor torque re-armed on wake and no retry of an unacknowledged physical move
- Robot volume is mapped to the hardware's dB-linear scale, fixing a bug where any non-maximum volume made the robot inaudible; the official cue sounds are uploaded to the robot
- State-driven physical expressions replay the official recorded emotion and dance libraries through a hardware-screened whitelist, plus continuous liveliness (breathing, antenna sway, head glances with lagged body-yaw follow)
- "Robot motion" menu toggle turns physical expressions and liveliness off without disconnecting
- Virtual Reachy Mini in the 3D renderer, with the official rig, Draco decoder and Apache-2.0 cue sounds bundled offline; the renderer mirrors the physical robot's reported pose when one is connected
- Renderer now reads the current pet prefs on every reload, so switching robots never restores stale settings
- Source layout split into `src/state/`, `src/shell/`, `src/robots/duck/` and `src/robots/reachy/`, with a guard test that every `__dirname` path literal under `src/` resolves
- New guides: `docs/guides/reachy-mini.md` and the 2026-09-06 Reachy control audit; NOTICE credits the Pollen Robotics assets

macOS (arm64/x64 dmg+zip) and Windows (x64/arm64 NSIS).

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/Happenmass/duck-on-desk/compare/v0.1.1...v0.2.0

payload.title: 飞特版跟进请教：打印材料/质量、训练策略、HAT 板 PCBA、舵机参数 4 个问题
payload.body:
你好！我在按你的飞特 HD-1910 版做复刻，目标是做一只能走路 + 有视觉/语音对话 + 接云端 LLM 的鸭子。
读了 microduck-replica 和 CAD 仓的文档，受益匪浅，有 4 个问题想请教（按我的下单优先级排序）。

## ① 打印材料与整机质量（最急，我要找打印服务下单）

你在 `imu-fix-1015` 里写「整鸭带电池 **806 g**，训练用 820 g，差 1.7%」。
我算了一下：官方 737.2 g + 15 只舵机各重 4.5 g ≈ 804.7 g，对得上。
我想让整机质量尽量贴近你那台，以便直接复用你的实机数据，所以想确认这个 806 g 的构成：

1. **是全 PLA，还是部分件用了铝合金增强？**
   CAD 仓 BOM 里「颈部 / 躯干底座 / 上腿加固板」标注了「可换铝合金增强」——
   你实际打的是塑料还是铝？
2. **填充率（infill）是多少？** 这在 Bambu Studio 的 3MF 里有预设，
   我要找打印服务商打（他们只收 STL，拿不到 3MF 参数），需要知道具体数值。
3. 层高 0.2 / 0.4 喷嘴 / PLA Basic 这几个参数，确认一下我没理解错。

另外：你的 3MF 是 09-15 版，v2.1 改了 TPU 合体轮胎。
**我们这种不做轮滑的版本，是不是直接按 09-15 那 52 个对象打就行？**

## ② 走路策略：重训还是调参

看到你 10-15 的记录里**收回了「舵机不行，要重训」**这个结论，
说「大家好多用他的跑通了」，元凶是 IMU 姿态模式（chip → gyro）。想确认现在的判断：

1. **现成 kissqy V167 策略 + 飞特舵机，是不是直接能走？** 还是要改动作缩放/滤波？
   （你的记录里用了「动作缩放 0.9、头滤波 0.5、腿滤波 0.7」）
2. **你 `software/training/` 里的 `Mjlab-Velocity-Flat-MicroDuck-HD1910`，
   打算自己跑完整训练吗？** README 写「尚无本机实测通过的走路策略」
   「本次没有提交付费云端任务」。如果暂时不打算跑，我用 `--hf-jobs` 跑一版
   （官方说约 1–2 h / 十几元），训出来会发布回来给你。
3. 你提到「现有 Microduck 质量惯量仍是原版仿真值，后续需要按飞特实机数据校正」——
   **这个校正做了吗？** 还是仍用原版值？

## ③ HAT 板 / imu_to_dxl 板

看到 issue #25 有人问过套件，当时回答「舵机还没到」。现在应该到了，想再问一下：

1. **HAT 板 / imu_to_dxl 板有打样好的余量可转让吗？** 或者有没有拼单渠道？
   我们自己打样 4 层板 + SMT（113 个贴装位置、含 0603）起订量不划算。
2. 如果买不到，**嘉立创 PCBA 的 SMT 你走过吗？** 有没有踩过坑
   （哪些料要自己备、钢网要不要开）？

## ④ 舵机参数核对

你们和 LuwuDynamics 都用 `1910_m6.json`（`STS3215Actuator`）给 HD-1910 建模。想确认：

1. **HD-1910-C001 是否等同 HLS1910 / STS3215？** 飞特型号命名有点乱，
   XGO-Duck README 写 "HLS1910"，参数文件里写 `sts3215`。
   如果确认同族，我就直接沿用 `1910_m6.json`；否则要做系统辨识。
2. **规格书上的 10 kg·cm 是在几伏下测的？** `1910_m6.json` 里的 `kt` 隐含电压假设，
   我们总线是 6.6–8.2 V（满电 8.4 V），想核对匹配。
3. 减速比、编码器分辨率、回差这三项规格书上没有 —— **你们实测过吗？**

（注：你文档里说「参数不是本项目自行辨识的结果」，所以这条也许没人答得上来 ——
那我就直接沿用并做实机对照。）

---

另外提一下我的扩展方向，如果你也在做可以一起搞：
除了走路，我还要加**视觉 + 语音对话 + 云端 LLM**（大致是 Reachy Mini conversation app 那套）。
有两个硬件问题想请教：

1. **HAT 上麦克风和喇叭的间距，自播报时的回声（AEC）好消吗？**
   我想做声纹识别主人/家人，如果 AEC 做不好声纹就废了。
2. 摄像头装在头里，**你那边出图正常吗？** 官方代码 `--rotate` 默认 90，
   你记录里写「摄像头调整排线后在官方 B1 下出图」—— 是转 90 还是 180？

非常感谢！有问题我也会把结果反馈回来。

tools: HD1910M 工具新增零位校准/重启指令与角度限制增强（作者：漂移菌）
payload.body:
## 概述

为 HD1910M 舵机测试工具补齐与飞特 FD 调试软件对标的**零位校准**与**活动区间限制**能力，并新增重启指令；已在 microduck 实机（15 颗 HD-1910，固件 3.46）完成全量验证。

作者：漂移菌

## 新增功能

### 1. 零位校准 `zero`（0x0B 位置校准指令）—— 核心新增

等同 FD 软件的"设置零位"按钮：把当前机械位置标定为指定读数（默认中位 2048），舵机自动修改 31 号位置偏移寄存器。

HD-1910（HLS 系固件 ≥3.43）**不支持**"扭矩开关写 128"的老式校准（回"成功"但不生效），0x0B 是本机型唯一正确的校准指令。命令内部走 解锁 → 校准 → 上锁 → **回读双重确认**（飞特的"成功"应答不可信，偏差 >4 单位即报错）。

```bash
feetech-HD1910M-tester torque off      # 松轴，手摆到机械零位
feetech-HD1910M-tester zero            # 当前位置 → 2048，掉电保存
feetech-HD1910M-tester zero --to 1024  # 或标定为任意读数
```

### 2. 重启命令 `reboot`（0x08）

等效断电重上电（SRAM 从 EPROM 重新加载），可**不物理断电**验证 EPROM 写入落盘——robotd 换舵机流程用的也是这条指令。

### 3. 协议层新增指令

`Reboot = 0x08`、`ResetTurns = 0x0A`、`Calibrate = 0x0B`，附组包单元测试。

## 功能增强

- `limits` 活动区间限制：新增 `--deg` 角度输入（`limits 90 270 --deg --save`）、`min < max` 交叉校验、多圈 `0 0` 特判放行、`--save` 单次解锁写两颗、写入后回读确认

## 修复与内部改进

- **修复 `set --defer` 异步写跳过范围校验**（越界值会被直接编码发出）；所有写入路径统一走新增的 `Register::check_value()`
- `ServoError::Malformed` 改为携带 `String`
- 新增单元测试，共 8 个全过

## 实机验证记录（15 颗 HD-1910，固件 3.46）

- 0x0B 校准实测：位置 2958（+80°）→ 精确 2048，偏移自动写入 910（= 2958−2048，实测确认偏移语义为"反馈值 = 原始值 − 偏移量"），掉电保存
- **0x08 重启在固件 3.46 实测可用**（`飞特适配架构.md` 台架待验事项可以划掉）
- 15 颗全量验收：ID 表、固件、字节序、波特率、应答级别、模式 4、电压窗口、卸载条件 13（电压+过热+过流）全部达标

详细变更见工具目录下的 `CHANGELOG.md`。

payload.title: MicroDuck Feetech Replica – Hardware, Firmware and Software Clarification Before Assembly
payload.body:
Hello,

My name is Gianluca, and I am building your MicroDuck Replica using the Feetech 3D-printing project (52 printed parts). I have already started printing the components.

Thank you for sharing your work and documenting your progress. I would like to reproduce your Feetech version as faithfully as possible.

Before purchasing the electronics and assembling the robot, I would appreciate your help confirming the current hardware and software configuration. I have read your repository and recent updates, but I want to make sure I follow the latest tested setup rather than an earlier design or a component that is still under development.

I hope to clarify the remaining questions in one message and avoid disturbing you repeatedly during the build.

1. Recommended hardware and electronics

Could you please confirm the exact hardware configuration you currently recommend for a new Feetech build?

Are 15 Feetech HD-1910-C001 servos still the correct model and quantity?

Is the Radxa Zero 3W still the recommended main computer? Is the 8 GB RAM / 64 GB eMMC variant compatible with your design and software?

Which controller boards, adapters and custom PCBs are required for the completed robot?

Which components have already been tested on your assembled Feetech robot, and which are still experimental or planned?

Is there an updated bill of materials (BOM) that reflects your current build?

2. Servo interface, connections and calibration

I understand that you successfully controlled all 15 Feetech servos using a Feetech URT-2 USB adapter.

Is the URT-2 also the recommended interface between the Radxa and the servo bus in the completed robot, or is it mainly used for testing and calibration?

How should the 15 servos be physically connected and powered?

Is a specific bus distribution board, adapter or wiring arrangement required?

Which wiring diagram and power-connection instructions should I follow?

Where can I find the latest servo ID mapping, joint directions, zero positions, standing positions and safe movement limits?

3. IMU and orientation feedback

I have read about the imu_to_dxl board and the recent firmware contribution by @Abo1ish. I understand that an initial firmware implementation has been tested and that IMU orientation can be displayed in the servo-web diagnostic interface through J-Link.

I also understand that the Feetech 15-byte bus protocol has not yet been implemented in that firmware.

Could you please clarify:

Which IMU hardware is installed in your current Feetech robot?

Which IMU solution do you recommend for a new Feetech build?

Is the imu_to_dxl board ready to build and use, or should I wait for a newer hardware or firmware revision?

Is the alternative BNO085 IMU connected directly to the Radxa still a recommended option?

Has either solution already been integrated and tested with the Feetech movement-control software, rather than only with the diagnostic interface?

Where can I find the current wiring instructions, firmware, software configuration and calibration procedure for the recommended IMU?

My aim is to install an IMU that the movement-control software can actually use.

4. Current movement software and capabilities

I have seen your video showing the Feetech robot standing up and sitting down. I have also read about your FeetechIo implementation and the current status of walking-policy training.

Could you please confirm which of the following capabilities have already been physically tested on your Feetech version?

Standing up and sitting down

Maintaining balance using IMU feedback

Walking forward

Turning while walking

Recovering after a disturbance or fall

Is the feetech branch of your MicroDuck fork currently ready to run on an assembled Radxa-based robot, or should a new builder initially use only the servo-web diagnostic console?

Does the Feetech version require a separately trained walking policy? If so, are the required model files already available, or is this work still in progress?

5. Operating system and first startup

I noticed your recent Radxa Zero 3W Armbian release and the documentation about boot issues on certain board revisions.

Which operating-system image and installation procedure do you currently recommend?

Are there any Radxa board revisions that require special attention?

Which instructions should I follow for initial servo configuration and calibration?

Is there a recommended first-start and testing procedure before enabling full-body movements?

6. Power supply and battery

For the initial build, I would like to follow the power configuration used in your working Feetech robot.

Could you please confirm:

The battery model, voltage, capacity and connector you currently use

The recommended power connection for the 15 Feetech servos

How the Radxa receives its regulated 5 V supply

Any required voltage regulators, distribution boards, switches or protection components

The correct power-on and power-off sequence

If available, could you please point me to your latest corrected wiring diagram?

7. Camera, distance sensor and audio

Could you please confirm the exact camera, distance sensor, microphone, speaker and audio interface or amplifier recommended for the current Feetech build?

I noticed that your recent documentation recommends the VL53L5CX instead of the VL53L8CX because of the mounting-hole dimensions of face_part. Is the VL53L5CX the correct choice for the Feetech printed parts?

Is the beak servo already independently controllable through the available software? If so, where can I find the corresponding command or documentation?

8. Current documentation and remaining work

Your project is progressing quickly, and I want to make sure I am using the latest instructions.

Could you please point me to the current recommended BOM, wiring diagram, firmware, software branch and assembly instructions for the Feetech version?

It would also be helpful to know which components or software features are still under development and should not yet be considered ready for a new build.

If these questions are already answered in your latest documentation, links to the relevant files would be more than sufficient.

Thank you very much for your time and for sharing your project. I appreciate any guidance you can provide to help me assemble and configure the Feetech MicroDuck correctly.

Best regards, Gianluca

payload.title: 将 J-Link IMU 姿态并入 servo-web，固件归入硬件目录
payload.body:
现有 `tools/servo-web/` 增加可选的 J-Link IMU 数据源：同一个 3D 鸭子以舵机回读驱动关节角、以 IMU 四元数驱动躯干姿态。未启用 IMU 时隐藏该区域，原有调试功能照常。

## 实现

- `python server.py --port COM5 --imu-jlink imu-jlink.json`：一个服务、原 `/ws` 追加 `type: imu` 消息，现有日志文件新增 IMU 分类。
- `--fake --imu-jlink ...` 可只接裸板；`--fake --imu-demo` 可完全无硬件检查。两种数据源在界面分别标记。
- 保留默认绕 Y +90° 安装方向、显示归零及原始姿态；断流/过期保留末帧并撤销实时状态，关节变换保持独立。重心显示标明为模型几何估计。
- 固件与 Keil 工程放在 `hardware/imu_to_dxl/firmware/`。只保留一个预编译 HEX；解码后固定 SHA 绑定已审核的 RAM 布局，连接后仍逐字节核对实板 Flash，无需仓库中的 BIN/MAP。
- 复用原模型、build_model.py、CDN 和现有硬件 PDF；不包含独立查看器、CMD 启动入口或 ZIP 打包脚本。
- 驱动及许可证保留。硬件说明按现有原理图校正 J3：SWD 使用1/2/3/6，第4/5脚为 UART_RX/TX，第6脚为 VTref。

## 验证

- `python selftest.py`：全部通过。
- `python -m pytest test_imu_bridge.py test_imu_server.py`：45 passed、59 subtests passed。
- `node --test test_imu_attitude.cjs`：13项全部通过。
- 迁移后 `Tools/test.ps1`：协议106项、IMU16场景、寄存器14项、Python4项全部通过；固件 Core/Drivers/Startup/Keil 和 HEX 未改逻辑或重新构建。
- 浏览器联合演示：模拟30号关节目标2048→2300、实际回读2297时，IMU躯干仍持续更新；归零、安装方向、原始姿态、IMU日志、断流显示均通过。以不带IMU参数重启后面板隐藏、15/15模拟舵机在线，原滑块仍可用。

## 范围

此次不连接真板或真舵机；尚未验证两者同时运行及现场轴向。原开发板此前验证过 J-Link 约20Hz读取，SDK建连可能重启板上程序。真实模式要求填写自己的DLL和探针序列号，`resume` 默认false，只有显式启用且固件验证通过后才能恢复暂停CPU。

**固件仍是早期 Dynamixel Protocol 2.0 / ID200 / 地址124的12字节基线，飞特地址56、15字节协议及 `imu200.py check` 留到下一步。** 姿态页面不测平移、不判断真实接触或整机平衡。详细记录见 `hardware/imu_to_dxl/firmware/VALIDATION.md`。

payload.title: 新增 imu_to_dxl v2 板 KiCad 工程（含 J2/J3 走线修复与 BOM）

## Summary

payload.title: imu_to_dxl 改版：25×25 mm，四角金属化 M2，双面地，附生产文件
payload.body:
这是 imu_to_dxl 的另一版设计，**不是现有 45×22 版的增量改进** —— 两版针对的
总线协议不同（本版是飞特 STS/SCS，现有版是 Dynamixel），零件不能互换，
请当作并列方案评估。

主要差异：

| | 现有 45×22 | 本版 25×25 |
|---|---|---|
| 板框 | 990 mm²，R2 圆角 | **625 mm²（−37%）**，直角 |
| 安装孔 | 2 × M2 非金属化 | **4 × M2 金属化 + φ3.0 GND 焊环**，孔距 20.17 mm |
| 铺铜 | 底层单面 | **双面** |
| 贴装 | — | **23 器件全顶层**，单面贴装 |
| 走线 | 333.6 mm，底层 19 段 | 219 mm，底层 18 段（占 19.6%） |
| 生产文件 | 无 | **Gerber + BOM + 贴片坐标** |

热布局：U3（LDO，唯一热源）与 U1（IMU，零偏最吃温度）对角布置，相隔 16.4 mm。

复查：EasyEDA DRC 0 违规；另用独立脚本重算间距、连通性与虚接 —— 18 个非 GND
网络全部单一连通，最薄关键接点 10.00 mil（同宽走线满宽对接）。

**仍未打样、未上电验证**，固件也没写。

待补：`.eprj2` 工程文件（嘉立创 EDA 的 API 导不出，需从界面手工导出）。

谢谢！这个 PR 分量很重 🦆 固件是仓库里最缺的那块，而且实板验证过、带主机测试（协议 106 项 / IMU 16 个场景 / 寄存器 14 项），`VALIDATION.md` 里把边界写得很清楚，特别是主动说明了"还没实现飞特 15 字节接口"，这点很难得。

想请你调整一下再合。**目标是把 IMU 姿态显示并进现有的串口网页 `tools/servo-web/`，而不是另放一份复制品** —— 这样调试台里的 3D 鸭子就能同时显示两样东西：关节角（来自舵机）+ 躯干姿态（来自 IMU），合起来就是整机真实姿态。

## 1. 固件 → `hardware/imu_to_dxl/firmware/`

- 整个 `firmware/imu_to_dxl/` 挪到 `hardware/imu_to_dxl/firmware/`，跟原理图、PCB 放一起
- `Build/imu_to_dxl.map` 删掉（编译产物，315 KB）；`.hex` / `.bin` 建议挂到 GitHub Release 上，不进源码树（或者只留一个 `.hex` 方便没装 Keil 的人直接烧）
- `Drivers/`（CMSIS、LSM6DSV16X 驱动）保留没问题，许可证你已经写清楚了

## 2. 查看器 → 并进 `tools/servo-web/`

**要删掉的复制品**（仓库里已经有了，逐字节相同）：

| 文件 | 仓库里现成的 |
|---|---|
| `servo-web-imu/model/meshes.bin`、`model.json` | `tools/servo-web/model/` |
| `servo-web-imu/build_model.py` | `tools/servo-web/build_model.py` |
| `硬件资料/imu_to_dxl-原理图.pdf`、`PCB.pdf` | `hardware/imu_to_dxl/` |
| `vendor/three.module.js`、`OrbitControls.js` | 调试台从 CDN 加载，跟着用就行 |

**要并进去的**：

- `imu_bridge.py` + `test_imu_bridge.py` → 放进 `tools/servo-web/`（比如叫 `imu_jlink.py`）。这是你写的核心，原样搬过去
- `server.py` 加一个可选参数，比如 `--imu-jlink config.json`：给了就起你的 bridge 线程，姿态数据走调试台**现有的 WebSocket**（新加一种消息 `{"type": "imu", ...}`），不另开服务、不另开端口
- 日志用调试台现有的 `log(msg, cat, level)` 约定（分类可以新加一个「IMU」），这样出问题都在同一个日志文件里，能对着时间线查
- `imu.html` 里的姿态显示并进 `index.html`：3D 鸭子的**躯干**按 IMU 四元数转，关节照旧按舵机读数转。安装方向（`DEFAULT_MOUNT` 绕 Y +90°）和归零按钮保留
- 没接 J-Link 的时候这块就不显示，调试台其它功能照常

**建议先不进主仓库的**：三个 `.cmd` 启动器、`package.py`、`PACKAGE_FILES.txt`、分享 ZIP 那套。给队友打包分发的需求可以另外做，主仓库里调试台统一用 `python server.py` 启动。

## 3. 文档

- 顶层 `README.md` 和 `software/README.md` 的改动跟着新位置改：固件的说明放 `hardware/imu_to_dxl/README.md`，查看器的用法放 `tools/servo-web/README.md` 加一节
- `VALIDATION.md` 很好，建议保留在固件目录里

## 4. 合并前自检

```bash
cd tools/servo-web
python selftest.py          # 调试台自带的自检，现在 36+ 项，要全过
python -m pytest test_imu_bridge.py
```

固件协议层改成飞特那套以后（ID 200、地址 56、15 字节，规格在 [`hardware/imu_to_dxl/总线协议.md`](https://github.com/fanhao375/microduck-replica/blob/master/hardware/imu_to_dxl/%E6%80%BB%E7%BA%BF%E5%8D%8F%E8%AE%AE.md)），调试台就能**直接从舵机串口总线读 IMU**，不用 J-Link 了 —— J-Link 那条路留着做裸板调试。

合并了，感谢！🦆 set-id 这个确实是刚需，总线舵机出厂全是 ID 1，不改 ID 根本没法多颗挂一条总线。

有个小地方我合并后顺手跟了一个提交（6f361de），跟你说一声：三步里最后那步「重新锁定」要发给**新 ID**。因为写完 ID 那一刻舵机就只认新 ID 了，再发给旧 ID 就没人收，舵机会停在 EEPROM 解锁状态（55=0），之后误写 EEPROM 寄存器都会永久生效。而且结尾 `ping(new_id)` 照样成功，看起来是「修改成功」，不容易发现。飞特官方 Python SDK 也是 `unLockEprom(旧ID)` → 写 ID → `LockEprom(新ID)`。顺手加了回读锁标志确认。

另外分享一个我们在 Python 版踩过的相邻坑：**改 ID 那一包的应答可能用新 ID 回来**，所以那一包别等应答，不然会报「等 id X 的应答，来的是 id Y」。

## 概述

     在 `tools/` 下新增一个用 Rust 编写的 STS3215 总线舵机命令行测试工具，
     与现有 `tools/servo-web`（Python 网页调试台）互补：servo-web 适合可视化调试，
     本工具适合在终端里快速做上电检查、批量测试和 CI 式的 PASS/FAIL 判定。

     ## 功能

     - `scan`：扫描总线（带进度条），列出型号 / 当前电压 / 电压保护范围 / 温度保护
     - `info`：一次读回位置、速度、负载、电压、温度、电流、报警状态
     - `read`：读任意寄存器地址（学习、调试内存表用）
     - `raw`：打印原始收发字节（排查接线 / 波特率 / 回显问题用）
     - `move`：转到指定位置，可指定速度/时间
     - `test` / `test-all`：批量测试——中位→低位→高位→回中位置扫描，
       运动中每 20ms 采样，统计峰值电流、峰值负载、最大位置偏差，输出汇总表和 PASS/FAIL

     ## 实现说明

     - 不依赖第三方舵机库，自行实现最小 STS/SCS 协议（帧打包、校验和、
       ping、读写、状态解析），代码约 300 行，全部中文注释，便于学习
     - 寄存器地址已逐条对照官方 SDK `sms_sts.py`（FTServo_Python）核对：
       型号=3、ID=5、波特率=6、力矩=40、目标位置=42、当前位置=56、电流=69 等
     - 运动指令按官方 `WritePosEx` 方式从加速度寄存器起一次性写 7 字节
     - 处理了带报警舵机的 ping 应答与部分转接板 TX/RX 回显无法区分的问题
       （首包疑似回显时等待第二包，超时则以首包为准）

     ## 测试情况

     在 Raspberry Pi 5 + 飞特官方 URT 转接板（CH340，/dev/ttyUSB0，1M 波特率）
     + STS3215（7.4V 版本）上实测：

     - 4 个目标位置全部到位，最大位置偏差 1 步（约 0.09°）
     - 峰值电流 84~91mA（空载扫描）、峰值负载 38.8%
     - 供电 9V 时正确识别并报告过压报警（error=0x01，电压上限 8.0V），
       换回 7.4V 后报警消失、测试 PASS

     ## 依赖与构建

     - 唯一第三方依赖：`serialport = "4"`（Linux 下需 `libudev-dev`）
     - `cargo build --release` 即可，树莓派上首次编译约 1~2 分钟

     ## 备注

     - 使用时舵机需独立供电（7.4V 版接 7.4V，12V 版接 12V），不可从 USB 取电
     - 详细用法见 `tools/sts3215Servo_testtool/README.md`

## 链接确认

深圳飞特舵机工厂店（官方），标题就写着「机器鸭具身智能开源AI专用」。点开 SKU 后实价：

- **HD-1910-C001 ¥123**，免运费，预售 7 天内发货
- 同一个链接里还有 **FE-URT2-C001 调试板** 的 SKU，可以一起下单

15 只 ≈ **¥1845**。对比 XL330 淘宝 ¥235–238 × 15 ≈ ¥3570。

## 厂家规格书数据（对比 XL330-M288-T）

| 项 | XL330-M288-T | HD-1910-C001 |
|---|---|---|
| **电压范围** | 3.7 – **6.0** V（推荐 5.0） | **5 – 8.4 V** |
| **外形** | 20 × 34 × 26 mm | **34 × 20 × 23 mm** |
| **重量** | 18 g | **22.5 ± 2 g** |
| **堵转力矩** | 0.52 N·m @5V | **10 kg·cm ＝ 0.98 N·m** |
| 空载转速 | ~103 RPM @5V | 110 RPM（0.09 s/60°） |
| 额定负载 | — | 3.0 kg·cm ＝ 0.294 N·m |
| **堵转电流** | ~1.5 A @5V | **1.8 A** |
| 额定电流 | — | 500 mA |

**尺寸几乎一致**（前两维就是同一组数，第三维反而薄 3 mm）；**15 只累计重 +67.5 g**。

## 电压这条值得单说

Microduck 的舵机总线是**电池原压 6.6–8.2 V**，没有任何降压 —— 官方 HAT 原理图里
J13/J14/J3/J11 四个 Dynamixel 接口的电源脚全接 `+BATT`，整块板只有一颗 buck，
那路 5 V 是给主控的。

所以 **XL330 是被超压运行的**（额定上限 6.0 V，超出约 37%），而 HD-1910 的
5–8.4 V **完整覆盖这个区间**。同一套供电，一个是妥协，一个是额定匹配。

⚠️ 但要注意：**满电 8.4 V 恰好等于 HD-1910 的上限，零余量。**

## 协议：架构不用改

飞特 STS/SCS 有自己的批量读指令 **`SYNC READ`（`0x82`）**，用法与 Dynamixel 一致，
所以「把 IMU 做成总线上第 16 个设备」这套在飞特上同样成立。

而且两边的**应答机制是一样的** —— 官方运行时用的是普通 `sync_read`（全库检索
`fast_sync_read` / `0x8A` 零命中，`duck-control/src/bus.rs:236` 是 `sync_read_raw_data`），
每个设备各回一个独立包。

有意思的是出厂默认值反过来对飞特有利：STS 内存表第 7 号 **Return Delay Time 默认 0**，
备注还写着 "Not functional on STS"；而 XL330 出厂是 250，即 **500 µs/设备**，
官方源码原文「Across 16 devices that is 8 ms per tick — 40% of a 20 ms budget」，
必须手动写 0 才能消掉。

## 规格书还缺的四项，谁能问到麻烦补一下

1. **10 kg·cm 是在几伏下测的** —— 最要紧。若为 @8.4 V，电池掉到 6.6 V 时约降到 0.7 N·m。
   直接决定策略重训的力矩模型
2. **减速比** —— XL330 是 288.4:1，BAM 执行器辨识模型里这是关键项
3. **编码器分辨率** —— 口头称 12-bit，规格书上没有
4. **回差（backlash）** —— MJCF 有专门的 `*_backlash` 建模变体

另外提醒一个电流上的事：**堵转 1.8 A × 15 ＝ 27 A**，而 HAT 的 Dynamixel 接口
旁注是「3A max」。XL330 的 22.5 A 同样超 —— 这不是换舵机才有的问题，是本来就该核算
而一直没人算的。多关节同时大电流的动作（起身、摔倒自恢复、踢球）要留意线径和分配。

感谢！这个 PR 的工作量很实在 —— 原理图、布线、Gerber、钻孔文件、贴片坐标一整套，还写了 `route.py` 自动布线脚本。几个关键选型也判断得很准：

- **`MCP1703A`（耐 16V）** —— 总线满电 8.4V，很多参考设计在这里选了 5.5V 的 LDO 会直接烧，你这个选对了
- **BOOT0 用 R1 下拉** —— TSSOP-20 上 BOOT0 与 GPIO 复用，这个隐患你想到了
- **SWDIO=PA13 / SWDCLK=PA14** —— 接对了
- **`SN74LVC1G125` 单缓冲 + RX 直接监听总线** —— 比双缓冲方案更简洁，是 Dynamixel 从机的常见做法

不过有几处需要修，其中第 1 条会导致板子做出来 **IMU 完全不响应**，麻烦重点看一下。

---

## 1. ⚠️ U3 (LSM6DSV16X) 引脚定义错位 —— 必须修

自制符号 `imu_to_dxl.kicad_sym` 里，**后四个引脚的定义与实际芯片不符**。

对照 ST 官方数据手册 **DS13510 Rev 1，第 10 页 `Table 1. Pin description`**：

| 脚 | 数据手册 | 当前符号 | |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `SDO/SA0` | `SDO/SA0` | ✅ |
| **2** | `SDx/AH1/Qvar1`（**辅助**接口） | `SDX` | ❌ |
| **3** | `SCx/AH2/Qvar2`（**辅助**接口） | `SCX` | ❌ |
| 4–10 | INT1 / Vdd_IO / GND / GND / Vdd / INT2 / OCS_Aux | 一致 | ✅ |
| **11** | **`SDO_Aux`** | `SCX_Aux` | ❌ |
| **12** | **`CS`** | `SDX_Aux` | ❌ |
| **13** | **`SCL`**（SPI 时钟 SPC） | `SDO_Aux` | ❌ |
| **14** | **`SDA`**（SPI 数据输入 SDI） | `CS` | ❌ |

根源应该是把 **主接口和辅助接口搞混了**。ST 的命名确实容易误导 —— `SDx`/`SCx` 看着像 SDA/SCL 的变体，但它们是**外接传感器集线器**用的辅助接口；主 SPI 反而叫 `SCL`/`SDA`（13/14 脚）。

数据手册对 2/3 脚在 Mode 1 下的说明原文是：

> *Connect to Vdd_IO or GND if the analog hub and Qvar are disabled.*

**当前接法的实际后果：**

```
SPI_MOSI → 脚 2    接到了辅助接口
SPI_SCK  → 脚 3    接到了辅助接口
SPI_CS   → 脚 14   接到了 SDA（主数据线）
脚 12 (CS)、脚 13 (SCL) —— 悬空
```

SPI 三根线全部接错，两个关键脚悬空，**IMU 不会有任何响应**。而且现象是「能上电、能烧录、就是读不到数据」，很难排查。

**建议改法：**

```
SPI_CS   → 脚 12   (CS)
SPI_SCK  → 脚 13   (SCL)
SPI_MOSI → 脚 14   (SDA)
SPI_MISO → 脚 1    (SDO/SA0)   ← 不变
脚 2、3  → 接 GND（按手册建议）
脚 10、11 保持悬空即可（手册允许 leave unconnected）
```

---

## 2. ⚠️ 缺 CS 上拉电阻

数据手册对 12 脚 `CS` 的说明：

> *1: SPI idle mode / I²C · MIPI I3C communication enabled;*
> *0: SPI communication mode / I²C · MIPI I3C disabled*

**CS 电平决定芯片上电后进 SPI 还是 I²C 模式。** 目前全板只有 R1 一个电阻（用于 BOOT0 下拉），CS 没有上拉，上电瞬间在固件配置之前处于悬空状态，进哪个模式不确定。

建议加一个 **10kΩ 上拉到 +3V3**。

---

## 3. ⚠️ DRC 实际有 23 条违规，其中 9 条是真问题

PR 描述里写的是「0 条真实违规」，但提交的 `imu_to_dxl_drc_violations.json` 里统计如下：

| 类型 | 数量 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| `shorting_items` | **3** | 短路 |
| `clearance` | **3** | 间距不足 |
| `solder_mask_bridge` | **2** | 阻焊桥 |
| `tracks_crossing` | **1** | 走线交叉 |
| `silk_edge_clearance` | 6 | 丝印越界（可忽略） |
| `lib_footprint_mismatch` | 4 | 封装库不一致（可忽略） |
| `silk_over_copper` | 4 | 丝印压铜（可忽略） |

前四类共 **9 条**需要处理，尤其是 3 处短路 —— 带短路的板子不能投产。是不是最终版本没重新跑一次 DRC？

---

## 4. 💡 建议：连接器换成 JST EH 2.5mm

目前 J1/J2 用的是 `JST_PH_S3B-PH-K`（**2.0mm**）。

Pollen 官方的 RPI Robot HAT（[`elec_RPI_Robot_HAT`](https://github.com/pollen-robotics/elec_RPI_Robot_HAT)）上，Dynamixel TTL 接口 J13/J14 用的是 **`B3B-EH-A`（JST EH 2.5mm，立创 C160259）**。

换成同一型号的话，线束可以和官方 HAT 直接互通，不用做转接线。

---

## 5. 💡 板框尺寸

当前板框 **40 × 30 mm**。这块板要装进躯干内部，空间比较紧张，如果布局上还有优化余地，缩小一些会更好安装。

---

再次感谢这份工作 —— 除了 U3 那处引脚，整体架构、选型和 MCU 侧的连接都是对的，改完就是一版可以投产的设计。如果需要，我可以把 ST 数据手册的引脚表页面单独发出来对照。

payload.name: 复刻镜像 20261023c · Feetech / DXL2 IMU 自动识别
payload.body:
**免费，只供个人学习和非商业复刻，不随任何收费产品分发。** 镜像中的走路和动作模型适用作者的个人非商业许可，不得随 HAT、整机、套件等产品预装或分发，不要售卖烧好的卡，也不能用于收费服务。具体许可见附件 `microduck-replica-20261023c-models.txt`。

20261023c 为正式新版镜像：DXL 2.0 IMU 兼容已接入实际运动主程序和标定流程，默认自动识别支持的总线格式，Studio 显示实际识别结果。

补充兼容核验（2026-10-23）：已核对 [ScrapMeta 的 imu_to_dxl 固件](https://github.com/ScrapMeta/microduck-diy/tree/db04d323caa053ae0c96629268392cdbe7dc8b4f/imu_to_dxl/firmware)。其默认 DXL2 / ID 200 / 1 Mbps / 124-12 数据格式已由本版现有运行程序支持；对方真实 C 协议实现与本版 Rust 读取路径的 7 项串口仿真核验通过。小板需预先刷好与实板匹配的固件，镜像不会自动刷写 MCU；真实小板验收仍待进行。本次补充兼容说明，镜像附件和校验值保持原样。

## 本版内容

- **Feetech 总线 IMU**：识别 FT6、兼容的 IMU-to-DXL Feetech 固件，保留原来的数据格式和回复顺序。
- **DXL 2.0 总线 IMU**：支持 ID 200、124/12 SFLP 数据布局。IMU 和 15 颗 Feetech 舵机由同一个程序依次查询，共用采集时限。
- **默认自动识别**；也可在 `[bus]` 中用 `imu_protocol = "feetech"` 或 `"dxl2"` 固定协议。探测不修改芯片 ID、波特率或 EEPROM。
- **换协议后重新校准**：旧 Feetech 的安装方向确认不能直接授权 DXL2 上力。Studio 会清除不再适用的采集结果，小助手保留实际协议绑定；重新标定和恢复流程仍可使用。
- **显示真实信息**：页面区分协议、布局及身份；DXL2 没提供的芯片计数器、状态位和芯片侧数据年龄不编造数值。
- 保留 I²C BNO08x / LSM6DSV16X、初次站姿采数、IMU 重新标定、模型管理与传感器页面。模型和其他 daemon 沿用已核验版本。

支持的是上述协议和数据布局，**不是所有厂家的任意 IMU 固件**。其他寄存器格式、ID、波特率需要适配。更换物理模块或安装方向后，即使协议相同也应重新校准。

## 验证范围

- Studio 最终功能版本完整测试共运行 1,037 项，4 项跳过，其余通过；其中协议相关的后端、小助手和浏览器回归 151 项通过。
- 控制核心 251 项、参数 110 项、单实例/更新健康门控集成测试 18 项通过；包含 19 项 DXL2 与混合串口测试。
- robotd 单元测试逐项独立运行：新版 296 项通过、2 项跳过、17 项失败；原提交相同条件下有相同的 17 项失败，没有新增失败。新增 DXL2 完整标定及故障停止流程通过。
- 镜像脚本 117 项在 Linux root 下通过；交付文件完成 SHA256、xz、独立解压、分区和 ext4 只读检查，核对实际 robotd、Studio、小助手及出厂状态。
- **新增总线兼容尚待真板验收**，没有连接或修改你的鸭子。摄像头默认仍为测试画面，按硬件自动启停摄像头/ToF 服务未在本次实现。

## 下载和源码

- SHA256：`10009c0a4aa963900719649836f5544036ad52cc15e3a0228eef05f6b747dab5`。
- Studio / 镜像冻结源码：`dd7a753026c40b0bf385374a896e7253cff42720`。
- [runtime 源码](https://github.com/fanhao375/Microduck-kissqy/tree/0791fcd44f71c705dc8bb0fbcde405593b52d19b)：`0791fcd44f71c705dc8bb0fbcde405593b52d19b`，build `4734cbb-feetech-imu-auto-control.44`。
- robotd SHA256：`edf182edb7bf11aeeeedfdab98170ab2ec48a9ec18417f9b68c744b0a60c6d16`；小助手 0.7.1。
- 附件六份：镜像、校验值、manifest、licenses、third-party、models。

20261023b 是新版正式镜像，修复初次 IMU 安装方向标定不接受已站稳的站姿使能的问题。已通过软件回归及交付镜像离线核验；这一版仍需真实鸭子上的新卡装机、标定和行走验收。

## 本版修复

- 第一次标定 IMU 安装方向时，可以手动点「站姿使能」，等 HOME 姿势站稳后，双手扶住鸭子采静止和前倾。也保留卸力后托住采数的方式。
- 只有标定模式下明确站稳、全部上力、HOME 误差不超过 5°，且没有运动、上电或卸力待确认，才接受站姿采数；起身中、部分上力和状态不明仍拒绝。
- 采数、计算和主程序验证沿用原有流程，不自动上力或启动行走。切换运行模式的重标定恢复会话仍要求卸力；舵机零位、方向和限位不变。
- 保留 20261023 的模型导入/命名/切换/改键/恢复默认、摄像头与 ToF 页面、七项设备状态，以及 IMU 重新标定和恢复功能。

## 初次 IMU 标定

1. 先核对舵机装配位置和方向，双手扶好鸭子，在 IMU 页点「站姿使能」，等它站稳。标定模式只锁住关节，需要一直扶住。
2. 把实物摆正，点「采静止（3 秒）」；再让整个躯干前倾 15–30°，停住后点「采前倾（3 秒）」。
3. 对照安装方向确认。**点击「交给主程序验证」前先把实物回正并停住**，点了以后按提示再次前倾。
4. 初次方向验证后，还可以做「站着校准」精校。

## 验证范围

- IMU 后端与计算检查 86 项通过，重标定小助手检查 21 项通过。
- 最终发布源码的完整浏览器流程 10 项全部通过，包括卸力粗校、站姿粗校、运动模式站立、重标定恢复和失败回滚。
- 最终 `.img.xz` 通过 SHA256 和 xz 校验，独立重新解压后的分区及 ext4 只读检查通过；337 个 Studio 文件与冻结源码一致，39 个运行时/模型文件哈希匹配，helper 0.7.0 和 sudoers 已核对。
- 出厂保持标定模式、15 颗未标定零位；机器身份、SSH 主机钥匙、开发者登录钥匙、Wi‑Fi 和私人运行状态已清理。
- 摄像头默认仍是测试源；真实摄像头与 ToF、按硬件自动启停服务、以及这一版整机实测的边界与上版相同。自动启停策略尚未实现。

## 下载

适用于 **Radxa Zero 3W + 飞特 HD-1910**。下载 `.img.xz` 和同名 `.sha256`，校验后用烧录工具写入已备份或空白的 TF 卡。开机连接鸭子热点，打开 `http://10.42.0.1:8000/`，按上手清单操作。

- SHA256：`72742592771652684d9b175e58f77a2b06d746f42fb5f57af099d1d44fe5cf3c`。
- Studio / 镜像构建源码：`320540ed510c0380b1d01b0cb8187f2c1e6d197e`。
- 主程序保持 fork 提交 `4734cbb0aac075335ef206d6557d0b6a3eb9e0a9`；robotd SHA256 为 `ead7f2f8aa5f24cb9883a976f7b23f8184d11ae26aa109afdaf5fe132660c1d1`。

> **新版入口：20261023c** — [下载正式最新版、校验值和更新说明](https://github.com/fanhao375/microduck-replica/releases/tag/microduck-replica-image-20261023c)。主程序新增 Feetech / DXL2 IMU 自动识别；新增硬件兼容待实机验收。本页面和附件保留为旧版。

>

## 这一版新加的（跟 20261021 比）



- **新卡热点马上开**：一个 WiFi 都没存过（新卡第一次开机），断网那一拍就开热点，以前要白等 45 秒。

- **SSH 能登记钥匙**：「更多」页的 SSH 卡片，除了自己定密码打开，也能把自己电脑的公钥贴进去，不开密码登录也能 SSH。卡片上写了 Windows / Mac 怎么生成钥匙。

- **双击「跳过」不误点**：以前确认按钮冒出来会把同一行的按钮挤开，双击「跳过」的第二下会落在「已完成」上。

- **总线 IMU 也认我们自制的板**：除了 kissqy 的 FT6 小板，也认本仓库的 imu_to_dxl 板（固件 0.2.0、1.0.0 都行）。主程序把它排在一次读全身的最后，排第一会跟舵机撞包。

- **主程序**（我们的 fork）：

  - 标定模式第一次读到舵机以后，清掉启动报告。以前 Studio 永远显示「主程序启动中」，拿不到读数；

  - 标定模式新加「站姿使能」：15 颗舵机 3 秒一起转到站姿，锁住。

- **上手清单**：每一步都是「去做 / 已完成 / 跳过」，任何时候都能点，只提醒后果。跳过 IMU 那一步，第 3 步按默认装法写，跳过第 1、2 步也能进运动模式。

- **IMU 页**：标定模式下也能「站姿使能」，站着校 IMU，不用先写进主程序；「现在」那块在标定模式下也有倾角和读数。

- **连 WiFi**：点了连接以后，页面自己找到鸭子的新地址，跳过去。连上以后按设备打开：

  - Windows：`http://duck-xxxx:8000/`，开着 Clash 也能开；

  - 苹果设备：`http://duck-xxxx.local:8000/`；

  - 安卓：用路由器里看到的 IP。

- **SSH 远程登录**（新）：出了问题自己登进鸭子修，不用重烧卡。Studio「更多」页先设网页登录密码，再**自己定一个 SSH 密码**打开，卡片上给出登录命令（比如 `ssh radxa@duck-xxxx`）。镜像里不带任何人的钥匙，也没有能远程登录的默认密码。顺带修好了 SSH 主机钥匙不生成、22 口拒连。



## 这是什么



一张烧好就能用的 SD 卡，给**飞特 HD-1910 版** Microduck（Radxa Zero 3W）用。装好的有：我们 fork 的主程序、走路和动作模型、Microduck Studio 网页中控、首次开机（起名、认 IMU、开热点）。



用法：烧卡 → 开机 → 手机连鸭子的热点 `Microduck-xxxx`（密码 `microduck`）→ 浏览器打开 `http://10.42.0.1:8000/` → 在 Studio 里填家里 WiFi → 照「上手清单」6 步走（舵机零位 → IMU 方向 → 写进主程序 → 配手柄 → 测急停 → 站起来走）。全程不用 SSH。



**一步一步怎么用**：[烧录和第一次使用](https://github.com/fanhao375/microduck-replica/blob/master/software/image/烧录和第一次使用.md)



## 附件



| 文件 | 是什么 |

|---|---|

| `microduck-replica-20261021b.img.xz` | 镜像，约 710 MB。不用解压，balenaEtcher 或 Raspberry Pi Imager 直接烧 |

| `microduck-replica-20261021b.img.xz.sha256` | 校验值：`1235cff97c24a315440672160531f81d758a8c2fd525cbd7b735c02cc867b922` |

| `microduck-replica-20261021b-manifest.txt` | 镜像清单：用的底图、主程序和 Studio 的版本，删了什么、加了什么 |

| `microduck-replica-20261021b-licenses.txt` | 开源许可说明（Armbian 底座、官方运行时、我们的 fork、Studio） |

| `microduck-replica-20261021b-third-party.txt` | 第三方组件（ONNX Runtime、Studio 的前端库和 Python 包等） |

| `microduck-replica-20261021b-models.txt` | 模型说明：每个模型干什么、对应哪个手柄键、作者和许可 |



## 要什么硬件



- 飞特 HD-1910 版鸭子：15 颗舵机 ID 配好，HAT 插好（C1、D1 版都行）。原版 XL330 的鸭子不要用。

- 躯干 IMU，二选一：

  - BNO085 或 LSM6DSV16X 模块，接 HAT 的 J5 或 40 针的 27 / 28 脚（D1 版 HAT 上要设成 0x6B）。LSM6DSV16X 推荐装法：模块 x 轴朝下、z 轴朝前，这样装 IMU 那一步可以直接跳过；

  - 舵机总线上的 IMU 小板：kissqy 的 FT6 小板，或者本仓库的 imu_to_dxl 板（固件 0.2.0 起）。

  - **第一次开机前接好。**

- microSD 卡 8 GB 以上（我们用 32 GB）。



## 里面的版本



- 系统底座：Armbian 26.2.1（Debian 13），内核 6.1.115-vendor-rk35xx；官方 Microduck 运行时 0.15.1。

- 主程序 robotd：我们 fork 的 `hd1910-v167-imu-autodetect` 分支，提交 `4734cbb`，sha256 `ead7f2f8…`。padd、mediad 跟 20261020 是同一份，从二号鸭上拉的。fork 地址见仓库首页「软件」一节。

- Microduck Studio 和镜像构建脚本：`f3927aa`，都在本仓库 `software/` 下。



## 要知道的



- 出厂时主程序跑**标定模式**。上手清单第 3 步「写进主程序」成功以后才切到运动模式，之后开机直接能站、能走。

- 「站姿使能」在标定模式下不管平衡，站起来以后要扶着。站着的时候不能写进主程序，先点「失能」。

- 热点密码大家都知道，Studio 默认又没有登录密码：在外面演示前，去 Studio 的「更多」页设个登录密码。

- SSH 出厂只认钥匙、不认密码，**镜像里不带任何人的钥匙**。想 SSH 进自己的鸭子：Studio「更多」页「SSH 远程登录」，自己定一个密码打开（这个密码也是 sudo 的密码），或者登记自己电脑的公钥。root 锁着。

- 电池没电**不会自动关机**（只在页面上警告），鸭子摔倒**不会自动卸力**。

- 第一次开机以后才接的 IMU，要用 SSH 运行 `sudo microduck-firstboot --detect-imu-only --force` 重新识别。

- 出了问题：在 Studio「更多」页点「导出诊断包」，到仓库开 issue 或发到群里，说一下卡在哪一步。



本镜像由 microduck-replica 项目制作，跟 Pollen Robotics、Radxa、Armbian、飞特都没有隶属关系。

一张烧好就能用的 SD 卡，给**飞特 HD-1910 版** Microduck（Radxa Zero 3W）用：我们 fork 的主程序、走路和动作模型、Microduck Studio 网页中控，以及首次开机（起名、认 IMU、开热点）都装好了。

Packaged for direct download — no need to clone the repository. --- ## 下载什么 / What to download | 文件 File | 内容 Contents | |---|---| | **`microduck-cad-assemblies.zip`** (32 MB) | 16 个 STL：整机单文件 + 15 个部件，**已应用世界变换**，单位 mm，附零件对照表

7 renders: 4 views + 2 labelled exploded views + 1 colour-coded reference | ## 为什么值得下 / Why this is useful 上游 `microduck_rl` 里那 47 个 STL **各自处在零件自身坐标系**，直接导进 CAD 会全部堆在原点重叠成一坨。本压缩包里的 STL 已经按 MJCF 的运动学树变换到位 —— **打开就是装好的样子**。 The 47 upstream STLs are each in their own part coordinate frame; importing them directly piles every part at the origin. The files here have the kinematic-tree transforms already applied — **open them and the robot is assembled.** 整机 **144 × 141 × 264 mm**，**737.2 g**，796,792 三角面。 ## 没装 CAD 软件？/ No CAD installed? 仓库里的 [`tools/stl_viewer.html`](https://github.com/fanhao375/microduck-replica/blob/master/tools/stl_viewer.html) 是个零安装的 WebGL 查看器 —— 浏览器打开，把 STL 拖进去就能看。 ## ⚠️ 重要提示 / Important **仿真网格不是制造文件。** 仿真只保证外形与惯量正确，**不保证配合公差、螺纹、热熔螺母座和走线空间**。直接打印大概率装不起来 —— 先打一两个小件试装验证。 **These are simulation meshes, not manufacturing files.** Simulation only needs outer shape and inertia; it guarantees nothing about fit tolerances, threads, heat-set insert bosses or cable clearance. # microduck-arena

Race a Microduck policy against every other policy, on a clock you can trust.

New to competing? Read [Train your first policy](docs/guides/train-a-policy.md),
then open **Training & rules** on your chosen challenge.

Submitted policies are evaluated **server-side** on a fixed course over five
perturbed seeds, at every commanded speed in the event's declared sweep, and the
best result is recorded. A time reported by a browser is a number in devtools;
this one reproduces on the Space's hardware (x86_64 Linux), and you can download
any published policy and race it yourself. Elsewhere — a Mac, or another
architecture — the same run gives different numbers: the servo model is chaotic
enough that a run diverges after a few seconds of simulated time, so a local time
is indicative, not the board's.

It runs two ways, and both are first-class:

- **Locally**, with no Hugging Face account, no OAuth and no network. The run log
  is a directory on your disk.
- **As a Space** (this repo is one). Same code path; its times are the
  board's, and a local run on other hardware gives indicative ones.

## Deploying to the Space

The source of truth is the GitHub repo
[`pollen-robotics/microduck-arena`](https://github.com/pollen-robotics/microduck-arena).
**Every push to `main` deploys** — `.github/workflows/deploy-space.yml` publishes
the tree to <https://huggingface.co/spaces/pollen-robotics/microduck-arena>.

`git push` to the Hub does not work here: it rejects binary files pushed through
plain git and asks for Xet instead, and this repo vendors a GLB, forty-odd STLs
and an ONNX policy. So the deploy goes through the Hub API, which speaks Xet
natively — the same script the workflow runs is the one to run by hand:

```bash
uv run python scripts/deploy_space.py            # publishes the working tree
uv run python scripts/deploy_space.py --dry-run  # shows what would go
```

The run log is not part of this. It lives in the `ARENA_DATASET` dataset repo,
which a deploy never touches, so the board and the standings survive every
redeploy — see *Running as a Space* below.

The Space rebuilds itself on each upload. Its own Docker build re-measures the
golden run and fails if the physics does not reproduce, so a broken build is
better than a silently wrong leaderboard.

## Releasing

A tag `vX.Y.Z` matching `version` in `pyproject.toml` builds the wheel — package, built site,
meshes — and attaches it to a GitHub release (`.github/workflows/release.yml`). That wheel is
what `microduck-challenges` depends on:

```bash
git tag v0.2.0 && git push origin v0.2.0
```

## Running as a Space

The container filesystem is ephemeral, so a Space needs somewhere durable to
keep the run log. Set two things in **Settings → Variables and secrets**:

| name | kind | value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ARENA_DATASET` | variable | the dataset repo that holds the log, e.g. `pollen-robotics/microduck-arena-runs` |
| `HF_TOKEN` | **secret** | a token with write access to that dataset |

Without both, the Space still boots and the board still works — but every
recorded run is lost the next time it restarts or wakes from sleep. A
published policy's `.onnx` is not at risk from this: it lives in the
publishing author's own Hub repo, not on the Space. `GET /api/health` reports
`"durable": true` once it is configured, and the startup log says `EPHEMERAL`
in capitals when it is not.

An entry arrives from `uv run publish --enter`, from the workshop or a shell,
with the entrant's Hugging Face token (in practice a write token, the one
`publish` uploads with). The Space asks the Hub's whoami-v2 whose token it is,
then drops it: it never stores or logs it. The site keeps Hugging Face OAuth,
scope `openid profile`, for signing in, votes and withdrawing one's own
entries. Entering the board takes a Hugging Face repo the
author published themselves, raced at a pinned revision, and the board's
`.onnx` link resolves straight to that repo. A `.onnx` in hand is raced locally with
`arena score <onnx> --event <id>` and entered with
`uv run publish --onnx … --enter --event <id>`; the site itself has no entry form.

## Social clips

Every published run gets two clips — landscape and vertical — and the Space
renders none of them. The moment a publish completes it launches an HF Job of
its own on its own image, which runs `arena clip <run>`: a headless Chromium
photographs the arena's stage frame by frame on the job's GPU, ffmpeg encodes
the video, and the job writes the clip into the dataset. That is why the image
carries Chromium, ffmpeg and the EGL dispatchers (`libegl1`, `libgles2`).

Measured on 2026-10-05 on a 386-frame sprint clip: 75 s on a **t4-small** job,
against 588 s in SwiftShader on the Space's own eight vCPUs and 553 s on a
sixteen-vCPU job; about a cent a clip. The publication page follows the job,
frame by frame from its log. When the Jobs API refuses a launch, nothing is
rendered elsewhere: the run stays owed — its `clips/<run>/pending.json` marker
is the list — and is launched again later, and at every boot.

| name | kind | value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CHROME` | variable | the browser binary, if not at one of the usual paths |
| `ARENA_CLIPS` | variable | `0` stops owing clips |
| `ARENA_CLIP_FLAVOR` | variable | the job's hardware, default `t4-small` |
| `ARENA_CLIP_NAMESPACE` | variable | the account that runs and pays for the jobs, default the Space's owner |
| `ARENA_CLIP_TOKEN` | secret | the token that launches the jobs, with `job.read` and `job.write` on that account; default `HF_TOKEN`. The jobs themselves write to the dataset with `HF_TOKEN` |
| `ARENA_CLIP_JOBS` | variable | jobs running at once at most, default 4 |
| `ARENA_CLIP_PARALLEL` | variable | layouts a job renders at once, default half its cores |
| `ARENA_CLIP_BACKFILL` | variable | `1` also owes a clip to every run that has none — the log as it stood before clips — newest first, behind fresh publishes; once caught up a boot finds nothing to do |
| `ARENA_ORIGIN` | variable | where the recorder's Chrome loads `clip.html`, if not this server's own loopback address |

Each event's `[clip]` manifest section tunes its framing, duration and sounds
— see `arena/manifest.py`.

To render one run's clips by hand — a historical run, or a retry — run
`arena clip <run_id> --store DIR`; with `ARENA_DATASET` set it writes to the
dataset, as a job does, and `ARENA_CLIP_GPU=1` draws on the machine's GPU.

## Recovering the board

The run log can be lost — without `ARENA_DATASET` and `HF_TOKEN` it lives on a
container filesystem that every redeploy wipes. The **policies** are not lost
with it: publishing writes each one into its author's own public repo, tagged
`microduck-policy` and carrying a `manifest.json`. So the board is re-derivable.

```bash
uv run arena recover --store ~/arena-board                    # every event
uv run arena recover --store ~/arena-board --event sprint-2m
uv run arena recover --store ~/arena-board --all-tagged       # the whole ecosystem
```

With `ARENA_RECOVER=1` the same reconciliation runs at every startup, in a
background thread so it never blocks the Space coming up. It re-races only what
is **missing**, keyed on the Hub revision, so on a durable store it costs one
listing and finds nothing to do — measured: a second pass over a full store
restores 0 runs in 6 s. It is off by default because the local path must keep
working with no account and no network.

Two limits worth knowing. It restores only what reached the Hub — a `Test` run,
or anything published before policies went to the Hub, left nothing to recover.
And times are **re-measured**, never read back: a ranking you cannot re-verify
is not one worth restoring.

One thing this deployment does NOT have yet:

- **Submissions are synchronous and CPU-bound.** One entry is 33 simulated runs
  — about 3 s on a developer laptop, and proportionally longer on a shared
  2-vCPU Space. It works; it is not instant, and there is no queue.

## Run it

Python 3.12 (`uv` installs it: `uv python install 3.12`).

```bash
uv sync
cd app && npm install && npm run build && cd ..
uv run arena serve --store ~/arena-board --user $USER
```

`arena serve` finds the built site in `app/dist`. A wheel of this package (`uv build --wheel`
after `uv run python scripts/bundle_frontend.py`) carries it inside the package instead, at
`arena/frontend/`, so an installed Arena serves its site with nothing else on disk; that is
what the release workflow attaches to a tag. After building a wheel, delete `arena/frontend/`
(`rm -rf arena/frontend`) — an editable install prefers it over every later `npm run build` of
`app/dist`.

Open <http://127.0.0.1:8000>.

The home page is the club: `Season standings` ranks players by the points
their publications earned (first publication on an event 100, each published
run 10 capped at three a day, beating your own best 25 once per event, and
250/150/100 while you hold a podium place), and `Pick your round` lists the
events. The chip top-right opens your page, `#/p/<user>`; the standings link
to everyone else's. Points are folded from the run log on every request, like
the board — `GET /api/standings` and `GET /api/players/<user>`.

## From the command line

```bash
uv run arena events

# The repo vendors one reference policy, so this works with no setup:
REF=arena/assets/policies/BEST_alpha_walking.onnx
uv run arena score $REF --event sprint-2m
uv run arena score $REF --event sprint-2m --user me --name reference --store ~/arena-board
uv run arena board --event sprint-2m --store ~/arena-board

# A stage event plays a command timeline (arena/timeline.py) instead of racing:
uv run arena score $REF --event got-a-talent --timeline timeline.json
```

## What a policy has to be

One ONNX file with a **61-D observation input** and a **14-D action output** — the
same contract `robotd` enforces on the real robot, so a policy the Arena accepts
will load there too. A wrong shape is rejected with the reason:

```
observation width is 51, expected 61
```

## The events

| Event | Rig | Course | Command |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sprint-2m` | legs | 2 m flat | 0.25 m/s forward |
| `roller-sprint-2m` | rollers | 2 m flat | 0.6 m/s forward |
| `hill-climb-1m5` | legs | 1.5 m at 8° | 0.25 m/s forward |

Locally the board shows **one row per policy**, so your own `v1` and `v2` race each other;
resubmitting the same name only improves that row. A deployed multi-user Space sets
`ARENA_RANK_BY=user` to show one row per person instead, and `arena board --rank-by user`
does the same from the command line.

An entry is scored as the **mean finish time over five perturbed starts**, with
any failure to finish counted at the event's time limit — so a policy that is
quick four times and falls once ranks below a steady one. The replay you watch is
the median finishing run, not the best.

Two things about the shipped reference policy are worth knowing before reading
too much into a time: it tracks about 44% of its commanded velocity, and below
roughly 0.2 m/s commanded it does not walk at all. Both are measured; see the
design doc's calibration table.

## Developing

```bash
uv run --extra dev pytest        # engine + API
cd app && npm test               # frontend units
cd app && npm run dev            # UI on :5173, proxying /api to :8000
```

`app/src/rig.js` and the vendored `app/public/robot/` assets come from
[the Microduck sandbox Space](https://huggingface.co/spaces/pollen-robotics/microduck-simulator)
at a pinned commit — see `arena/assets/PROVENANCE.md`. Re-vendoring can change
what a policy scores, so `RUNNER_VERSION` in `arena/constants.py` must be bumped
in the same commit.

## Design

- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-03-microduck-arena-design.md` — the design and every decision behind it
- `docs/probe-results.md` — measured cost of an evaluation
